items.title: Washington governor calls ICE 'out of control' after Seattle airport arrests
items.description: The governor of Washington state called US federal immigration agents “out of control” after they arrested two people at Seattle’s main airport on Saturday. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers have conducted raids across the United States, part of President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown , which has forged ahead despite a rebuke by voters at this month’s midterms . Video footage widely shared on social media on Saturday showed two people being apprehended by masked men at an airport jet bridge. ICE later confirmed it had detained two people it said had overstayed their visas. Washington Governor Bob Ferguson said the agency was “completely and totally out of control”. “Like many Americans, I’m outraged by masked agents, who do not identify themselves, dragging people off jetways as they board a flight, creating chaos in our communities,” Ferguson wrote on X. “Today’s actions at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport are just the latest example of ICE’s deeply un-American tactics.” Ferguson said at a news conference that the ICE agents may have broken a state law limiting facial coverings for law enforcement, and that he was looking into how they accessed the jet bridge. The federal immigration agency said its officers “conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an illegal alien from Mexico who overstayed his visa” on Saturday morning. The agency confirmed it had detained a second person whom it said would be charged with assaulting a federal officer, alleging she had thrown hot coffee on an ICE agent. “The individual… was identified as Sofia Hernandez Mejia, an illegal alien from Mexico and visa overstay. She was subsequently arrested as well,” ICE posted on X. Alaska Airlines, which operated the flight that Mendoza and Mejia tried to board, said on Saturday it was “concerned by this morning’s law enforcement action”. “Alaska Airlines is required to comply with applicable laws and regulations when interacting with law enforcement officials” but does not “direct or coordinate immigration enforcement activity”, the company added. The Port of Seattle, which operates the airport, said: “We are outraged about this morning’s incident involving ICE and two passengers.” This month, Trump appointed Stephen Miller , architect of his hardline immigration policy, as his new chief of staff. Miller faced widespread criticism after the deadly shootings of two protesters by immigration agents in Minneapolis in January — incidents that sparked mass demonstrations.

items.title: Amputee World Cup: Dr Mohammed Raii delivers 30,000 bonus, promises further $120,00 if Black Challenge win trophy
items.description: Ghanaian entrepreneur Dr Mohammed Raii has fulfilled his promise of US$2,000 to each member of the Black Challenge following their historic qualification for the final of the Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. Raii, founder of the Eezzy Group Foundation, has also pledged a further US$8,000 to every player if Ghana beat Morocco to lift the trophy. The Black Challenge secured their place in the final after defeating defending champions Türkiye on penalties in the semi-finals, following an intense 1-1 draw after extra time. Raii said he wanted to make his commitment clear before the semi-final to avoid the uncertainty and disagreements that can sometimes follow sporting achievements, particularly over promised bonuses. He also wanted the players to appreciate the significance of their achievement and recognise the sacrifices they had made in representing Ghana. The incentive comes as the Black Challenge prepare for another meeting with Morocco, their opponents in the final of the 2024 African Amputee Football Cup of Nations. The two sides will renew their rivalry on Sunday at San Juan de los Lagos, with Ghana seeking to cap their impressive campaign by winning the world title for the first time. Their rivalry has produced some memorable encounters, including the 2023 African Para Games final in Accra, where Ghana came from behind to beat Morocco 2-1. Mohammed Mubarik scored the equaliser before captain Richard Arthur Opentil netted the winner in extra time to secure gold for the hosts. That victory came between Ghana’s African championship triumphs in 2021 and 2024, further establishing the Black Challenge as one of the continent’s leading amputee football sides. Mubarik has continued to play a decisive role in the team’s World Cup campaign, scoring twice in Ghana’s 2-0 quarter-final victory over Egypt to secure a historic place in the semi-finals. Beyond his support for the Black Challenge, Raii has also demonstrated a commitment to para sports in Ghana. In July, his foundation committed GH¢800,000 towards Team Ghana’s campaign at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. “When the world talks about Ghana, we want it to be associated with excellence,” he said during the presentation, according to the Ghana News Agency. Raii has also called on the government, corporate organisations and sporting institutions to invest more in opportunities for people with disabilities to participate in amputee football and other para sports. He believes a lack of assurance about financial and institutional support continues to discourage some potential athletes from getting involved. For now, however, the focus is on Sunday’s final, where the Black Challenge have an opportunity to turn their historic run into a World Cup triumph — and earn another significant reward in the process.

items.title: Oyo APM to Tinubu: Nigerians need better living conditions, not name-calling
items.description: IBADAN—THE Allied Peoples’ Movement, APM, in Oyo State, yesterday, tackled President Bola Tinubu for purportedly attacking the party during the All Progressives Congress rally held at Mapo Hall, in Ibadan. Tinubu, who was in Ibadan on Saturday, took a swipe at the APM and Governor Seyi Makinde. He said: “We heard there is a certain group/faction called the ‘palẹmọ’ (Pack up) group. Don’t mind them; they are only waiting in vain; there is nowhere they are going.” However, the APM described the president’s remark as desperate distractions from the mounting realities confronting Nigerians and the glaring failures of governance. The party, in a statement by its Director of Communication/Spokesperson Campaign Council, Yinka Oladoyinbo, said: “We consider the expression a curious choice of words from a President whose administration has become synonymous with economic hardship, public frustration, political manoeuvring and an increasingly desperate search for electoral validation. “In Yoruba political parlance, ‘palẹmọ’ evokes the hurried gathering, packing or clearing away of belongings, sometimes suggestive of preparing to leave or carrying away what one can before departure. “Mr President may wish to explain why such vocabulary comes so readily to him. As the saying goes, it takes a master of a craft to recognise the language of fellow practitioners. And when an accuser points one finger at another, the remaining four are invariably directed at himself. “The APM will not be distracted by presidential name-calling. Nigerians are far more concerned about the cost of living, the purchasing power of their incomes, insecurity, unemployment, collapsing economic confidence and the daily struggle to survive than the linguistic theatrics of a campaign podium.” The party also warned that traditional rulers, irrespective of their political affiliations, remain ”fathers to all.” “The APM remains confident that Oyo voters will distinguish between political noise and credible leadership, between borrowed prestige and earned trust, and between the spectacle of power and the substance of governance,” the statement said. The post Oyo APM to Tinubu: Nigerians need better living conditions, not name-calling appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Alexander Zverev - Carlos Alcaraz en directo | Alcaraz supera a Zverev y conquista por primera vez el título de las ATP Finals
items.description: Carlos Alcaraz ha derrotado a Alexander Zverev este domingo en la final de las ATP Finals en Turín (Italia) . El murciano comenzó con un ritmo superior el encuentro y puso contra las cuerdas a su rival desde el primer punto. Salvó hasta tres bolas de break Zverev en su primer servicio. Y en el segundo turno de saque, Alcaraz hizo lo que ninguno pudo conseguir en todo el torneo: romper al alemán. Lo hizo hasta en tres ocasiones en la primera manga y, pese a que salvó varios bolas de rotura de Zverev y cedió un servicio, sacó adelante el set (6-2). En el segundo asalto parecía que Zverez igualaba el ritmo con un buen primer servicio, pero cuando llegó su segundo turno de saque, Alcaraz lo rompió con un break en blanco. Parecía que el murciano se iba a llevar cómodamente el segundo set e iba a finiquitar la final, pero con 4-3 cedió el servicio y Zverev se metió de lleno en el partido. Se igualó la contienda y la segunda manga abocó en un tie-break donde Carlos dio la estocada final tras levantar tres bolas de partido para su rival (6-2 y 7-6(7). Alcaraz ya es maestro a sus 23 años tras conquistar por primera vez este torneo.

items.title: Any talks with India on terrorism must be 'evidence-based', says Musadik Malik
items.description: Federal minister Musadik Malik said on Sunday that any dialogue between Pakistan and India on terrorism must be “based on evidence”. Malik is in New Delhi on a three-day trip to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, making him the first Pakistani minister to visit the neighbour since former foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari attended an SCO meeting in May 2023. Pakistan has repeatedly offered to hold talks with India to resolve outstanding disputes, including the water issue. In video clips shared by India’s ANI news agency on Sunday, Malik responded to queries from Indian media and stressed that he had repeatedly presented Pakistan’s stance before the reporters. “I am giving you a stable response that whenever discussions take place, they will be based on evidence, and they will certainly happen,” he affirmed, saying if New Delhi wanted a “lasting solution”. “You must also have some issues, [though] our issues are much greater than yours, and we also need a lot of evidence […] Whenever dialogue takes place, it will be based on evidence,” the climate change minister reiterated. Malik said Pakistan had repeatedly stated that evidence relating to terrorism could be presented through both bilateral and multilateral forums. “You may bring evidence; we also have evidence that we want to present,” he added. India’s foreign minister had said in June 2024 that his country wanted to “find a solution to the issue of years-old cross-border terrorism” with Pakistan. However, a military conflict between the neighbours last year has intensified tensions and escalatory rhetoric from India. In May 2025, a four-day confrontation between Pakistan and India was sparked by an attack on tourists in occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam, which New Delhi, without evidence, linked to Pakistan. Islamabad had strongly denied responsibility while calling for a neutral investigation . In another clip, Malik noted that India had invited a representative from Pakistan to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum , a multilateral event. “I am your guest. You invited me to a specific forum; I am present before you. I answered all those questions you asked about this forum,” the minister said, remarking that he had conveyed the “voice of my heart” to the people across the region through the forum. Malik stated, “You are today asking me questions for which you did not invite me. When you invite me for that question, I will appear. However, you first ought to invite me and say ‘we want to speak bilaterally with you’.” ‘Will speak on IWT when invited to do so’ The minister was also asked about his remarks on the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT), but said he would comment on the matter when invited to do so. “You have currently invited me to speak on topics about which I have already spoken, that when temperatures rise, climate is destroyed, Glofs happen. Glofs and glaciers are blind, they do not know whether to fall on the right or the left,” he said, highlighting the shared threat climate change poses to both neighbours. He further said, “You have called me for culture and civilisation [discussions]. I am your guest, you are my host […] You have asked me the same question a 100 times and I have responded to it a 100 times.” In his remarks at the SCO forum on Saturday, Malik had termed climate change an “enemy” of civilisations and pointed out its impact on South Asian countries that bore the brunt of climate destruction. Water and the IWT remain a contentious issue between Pakistan and India, following New Delhi’s unilateral abeyance of the accord in April last year after the Pahalgam attack, which was followed by the four-day military conflict between the two sides. Following India’s move, Pakistan termed any attempt to suspend its water share an “act of war”, noting the IWT had no provision for unilateral suspension. It later argued that New Delhi’s action was a violation of the 1969 Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties. Backing Islamabad’s stance, the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) on Aug 31 ordered New Delhi to uphold the IWT, declaring that the treaty remained fully in force, as India had no justification for ending or suspending the agreement. The IWT, brokered by the World Bank in 1960, allocates the three western rivers — Indus, Jhelum and Chenab — largely to Pakistan, and the three eastern rivers — Ravi, Beas and Sutlej — to India. The treaty has survived wars, crises, and political tensions for more than six decades and is considered a rare example of durable water-sharing cooperation between the two neighbours.

items.title: Départ massif des orpailleurs de la Guinée : L’économie locale de Siguiri s’effondre à grande vitesse
items.description: En Guinée, le départ massif des orpailleurs de la préfecture de Siguiri à la suite du durcissement des contrôles sur l'orpaillage illégal a plongé l'économie locale dans une crise profonde. Autrefois poumon commercial de la région, cette zone cosmopolite voit aujourd'hui ses marchés s'assécher, ses gares routières se vider et ses milliers d'acteurs économiques des chauffeurs de moto-taxis aux commerçants de proximité sombrer dans l'incertitude. Face à l'absence d'alternatives viables, toute l'activité économique de la Haute-Guinée tourne désormais au ralenti. Dans le Nord-Est de la Guinée, les étals des marchés et les artères commerçantes de Siguiri s'enfoncent dans un silence inhabituel. Longtemps considérée comme un pôle d'attraction majeur où des milliers de personnes affluaient pour l'exploitation de l'or et faisaient prospérer la région, la zone fait face à une rupture brutale de son activité. L'intensification des interventions gouvernementales contre l'orpaillage clandestin au début du mois de novembre a provoqué le départ en masse des travailleurs, entraînant une paralysie immédiate et sévère du tissu économique local. Les répercussions de cet exode touchent de plein fouet les travailleurs indépendants et les micro-entreprises de la région. Dans le district de Bouré-Kofilani, le secteur des transports subit un choc violent : le syndicat local compte plus de 17 000 chauffeurs de moto-taxis qui ont perdu la quasi-totalité de leur clientèle et peinent désormais à subvenir aux besoins de leurs familles. La situation est tout aussi préoccupante pour les commerçants de denrées alimentaires, à l'instar des vendeurs de viande grillée de Bouré-Balato qui accumulent les invendus et mettent aujourd'hui deux jours pour écouler ce qu'ils vendaient habituellement en une seule journée. Le dépeuplement rapide des localités minières laisse derrière lui un paysage de désolation économique. Sur le terrain, les agents humanitaires observent des cités qui se vident à vue d'œil, marquées par des départs continus en bus et minibus. Cette asphyxie économique suscite de vives inquiétudes au sein des organisations civiles et politiques : le collectif des Forces vives de Guinée a déploré l'absence de solutions alternatives viables proposées par les autorités pour soutenir les milliers de personnes dont la subsistance dépendait directement de l'orpaillage. L’article Départ massif des orpailleurs de la Guinée : L'économie locale de Siguiri s'effondre à grande vitesse est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Subsidy Removal: You can’t wish away Nigerians’ hardship, ADC-PCC tells Tinubu
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has tackled President Bola Tinubu over his insistence that Nigerians should forget fuel subsidy, accusing him of being insensitive to the economic hardship confronting millions of citizens. The Council said the President’s remarks exposed his disconnect from Nigerians struggling with rising food prices, soaring transportation costs, poverty and an increasingly unbearable cost of living. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC was reacting to Tinubu’s declaration at a rally at Mapo Hall, Ibadan, Oyo State, that fuel subsidy belonged to the country’s past. Ologbondiyan spoke during an interaction with youths in Lokoja, ahead of the Council’s presidential campaign rally in Kogi State. “The President appears more interested in being addressed as Mr President than in tackling the crushing realities confronting the people. He has demonstrated little or no concern for the suffering of ordinary Nigerians. “That explains his brash insistence that Nigerians should forget about fuel subsidy removal simply because, in his estimation, it belongs to the past,” he said. Questioning how the consequences of the policy could be dismissed when Nigerians continued to bear its effects, Ologbondiyan asked: “How can hardship, hunger and widespread poverty, which are direct consequences of the hurriedly imposed economic policies of the Tinubu administration, suddenly become things of the past when Nigerians continue to bear their devastating consequences every day?” The Council argued that subsidy removal was announced without adequate preparation, effective safety nets or meaningful measures to cushion its impact on vulnerable citizens. It said the policy had contributed to soaring transportation costs, unaffordable food prices, struggling small businesses and worsening poverty among households. “To ask Nigerians to forget a policy whose consequences they confront every waking moment is not only insensitive; it is an insult to their intelligence and a mockery of their suffering,” Ologbondiyan added. The ADC-PCC maintained that responsible leadership required acknowledging policy failures and making necessary adjustments to ease citizens’ hardship, rather than defending policies despite their consequences. Beyond the economic crisis, the Council accused the Tinubu administration of weakening critical democratic institutions, including the judiciary, security agencies, anti-corruption bodies and financial institutions, allegedly to advance the President’s second-term ambition. It warned that institutions established to safeguard democracy and protect the public interest must not be subordinated to the political ambitions of any individual. “Nigeria cannot afford a second term built on the ruins of its democratic institutions and the continued impoverishment of its citizens,” the Council declared. Describing the country’s economic difficulties as the consequence of poor policy choices, inadequate planning and a failure to prioritise citizens’ welfare, the ADC-PCC insisted that the situation was neither inevitable nor beyond remedy. It endorsed its presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, as the leader capable of reversing the economic decline, restoring investor confidence and rebuilding democratic institutions. The Council said an Atiku-led administration would pursue properly planned economic policies, effective social protection mechanisms and a more humane approach to governance. It urged Nigerians to use lawful and democratic means to reject Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, arguing that the coming election offered an opportunity to change the country’s direction. “Nigerians deserve a government that feels their pain, understands their struggles and takes deliberate steps to ease their burden, not one that dismisses their suffering or asks them to forget the circumstances that have made life increasingly unbearable. “In 2027, Nigerians will have the opportunity to change this narrative. The power to rescue the country and restore hope rests firmly in their hands,” the ADC-PCC said. items.title: Varma century in vain as Pakistan Shaheens down India A in Asia Cup Rising Stars clash
items.description: Pakistan Shaheens overcame a late challenge from Tilak Varma to beat India A by 48 runs in their Asia Cup Rising Stars match in Doha on Sunday, defending a total of 313 after bowling out their opponents with five balls to spare. Skipper Varma struck a century before becoming the last man dismissed for 100 off 149 balls, while Shahbaz Ahmed made 56 in a seventh-wicket stand that briefly revived India’s hopes. But Pakistan’s bowlers held their nerve in the closing overs, with Hasan Nawaz claiming three wickets and Ali Raza taking three for 56. India’s chase had begun to unravel after an explosive start from Abhishek Sharma. The left-hander made 70 off just 42 balls, hitting six fours and six sixes, but his dismissal at 93-3 in the 16th over left the visitors with considerable ground to make up. Pakistan’s spinners then tightened their grip. Sufyan Moqim bowled Kumar Kushagra for two before Hasan removed Rinku Singh and Suryansh Shedge, leaving India struggling at 129-6 in the 26th over. Varma, who had struggled to find the boundary during the middle overs, found support in Shahbaz. The pair added 112 runs for the seventh wicket, taking the score to 241 before Raza broke the stand by having Shahbaz caught by Hasan for 56 off 49 balls. Raza then bowled Vipraj Nigam for a duck, while Imran Randhawa dismissed Harshit Rana to leave India nine down. Varma reached his second century of the tournament, but the milestone offered little consolation as Ahmed Daniyal had him caught by wicket-keeper Rohail Nazir in the 50th over to seal Pakistan’s victory. Controversial toss Earlier, Pakistan had posted 313 after winning a dramatic toss and electing to bat on a slightly dry surface. The toss decision was initially called incorrectly by the match referee, who announced tails after Varma flipped the coin on Pakistan skipper Abdul Samad’s call of heads. Samad pointed out the error and the officials corrected the decision in Pakistan’s favour. The captains did not shake hands, continuing the protocol observed in recent encounters between the sides. Pakistan’s openers Shamyl Hussain and Maaz Sadaqat gave their side a flying start, putting on 66 for the first wicket. Shamyl made 33 off 23 balls before Ayush Badoni had him caught by Harshit Rana at short third. Rana then trapped Rohail leg-before for a duck, with Pakistan on 67-2. The exchanges between Rana and the Pakistan batters had added an edge to the powerplay, with the Indian fast bowler involved in heated verbal exchanges and giving Shamyl an animated send-off. Maaz and Hasan rebuilt the innings, with the former scoring 59 off 63 balls for his second successive half-century. Hasan went on to make 79 off 82 deliveries, while Farhan Yousaf’s 56 off 48 balls and Imran’s quickfire 23 helped Pakistan push past 300, which was proven enough for the side at the end.

items.title: Souveraineté et haute technologie : Le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré dote le Burkina Faso d’un joyau académique en 11 mois chrono
items.description: Conçue pour inscrire le Burkina Faso sur la voie de la souveraineté scientifique et industrielle, l’Académie technologique du Faso (ATF) est désormais prête à accueillir sa toute première promotion. Érigé en un temps record de 11 mois sur un domaine de 60 hectares dans la commune de Babray, ce complexe universitaire ultramoderne sous régime d'internat intégral sera officiellement inauguré ce lundi 23 novembre 2026 par le Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Rattachée directement à la Présidence, l'institution forme 250 jeunes lauréats scientifiques dans des filières stratégiques allant du génie civil au nucléaire civil. C'est une étape décisive pour l'histoire industrielle et académique du pays des Hommes intègres. Inspecté en décembre 2025 par le chef de l'État, le chantier de l'Académie technologique du Faso (ATF), implanté sur la voie de contournement dans la commune de Babray, a vu les engins entrer en action dès janvier 2026. Alors qu'un délai de réalisation de 12 mois était initialement prévu, il a suffi de juste 11 mois pour achever la première phase de ce complexe de 60 hectares sous un contrôle-qualité rigoureux. Ce lundi 23 novembre 2026, l'infrastructure est officiellement inaugurée par le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, scellant la concrétisation d'une ambition présidentielle majeure. Le nouveau campus a été conçu pour rompre définitivement avec les enseignements purement théoriques. En quelques mois, le site s'est métamorphosé pour accueillir des amphithéâtres connectés, des ateliers de pointe, une forge industrielle, une bibliothèque, une infirmerie et des infrastructures sportives. Fonctionnant sous un régime d'internat intégral, l'académie garantit l'hébergement sur place des étudiants comme des enseignants, créant un cadre de vie axé sur la discipline, la cohésion et l'excellence. Directement rattachée à la Présidence du Faso, l'institution prépare les élèves aux métiers de demain dans des secteurs clés tels que la métallurgie, le génie civil, la chimie industrielle et les métiers miniers, tout en ouvrant la voie au nucléaire civil, à l'aéronautique, à la cybersécurité et au digital. Pour intégrer cette école d'élite, la sélection a exigé un niveau académique exceptionnel. Dès juillet 2026, à la suite des résultats du baccalauréat, un processus rigoureux a permis de choisir 250 jeunes lauréats issus des séries scientifiques et techniques parmi des milliers de candidats. Soumis à une rigueur exigeante et encadrés par des formateurs chevronnés, ces pionniers ont vocation à concevoir les infrastructures futures, à piloter les transformations industrielles et à sécuriser les réseaux énergétiques et numériques du pays. En investissant sur son propre sol dans le talent de sa jeunesse, le Burkina Faso brise les chaînes de la dépendance extérieure. items.title: Man United suffer 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in Pochettino’s first match as coach
items.description: Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start as Manchester United manager after Liverpool struck twice inside the first 13 minutes against 10 men to set up a 4-0 win at Anfield. United never recovered from Leny Yoro’s controversial red card after just eight minutes as Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz quickly made Liverpool’s man advantage count. Teenager Rio Ngumoha rounded off a stunning individual with Liverpool’s third before Victor Munoz completed the rout. Defeat leaves United still rooted second bottom of the Premier League and gave Pochettino an early indication of the huge job he has ahead to restore the 20-time English champions to their former glories. Liverpool climb into the top four and within seven points of leaders Arsenal to rekindle faint hopes of challenging for the title. Pochettino answered United’s call after Michael Carrick was sacked last week after winning just one of the Red Devils’ first 10 league games in charge. The Argentine has been linked with a move to Old Trafford for a decade, but failed to make a strong first impression on the United fans. Pochettino’s bold team selection backfired with the centre-back pairing of Matthijs de Ligt and Yoro at fault for the game’s decisive moment. De Ligt, on his first Premier League start for nearly a year, let a long ball down the middle and go and allowed Alexander Isak to bear down on goal. The Swedish striker took a heavy touch before he was clipped by Yoro, but referee Sam Barrott still deemed the French defender had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity and produced a red card. Szoboszlai rubbed salt into United wounds by drilling home the resulting free-kick from the edge of the box. Moments later Ngumoha skipped past Diogo Dalot and crossed for Wirtz to hook a shot in off the underside of the bar. Having relegated Harry Maguire to the bench, Pochettino was forced to turn to the veteran centre-back just 22 minutes in to try and stem the bleeding. United lost 7-0 at Anfield three years ago and a switch to a back five helped avoid similar damage, albeit with the help of some wayward Liverpool finishing. Maguire made a brilliant block to deny Isak a third goal just before half-time. Bradley Barcola and Isak were guilty of wasting huge chances early in the second half. But Barcola’s blistering pace created Liverpool’s third just after the hour mark. The French international destroyed Lisandro Martinez for pace before picking out Ngumoha to slot home. Wirtz rounded off one of his best Liverpool displays since a £100 million move from Bayer Leverkusen last year with the assist for Munoz to crash home the fourth goal eight minutes from time. Liverpool fans rejoiced in their rivals’ pain with chants of “you are going down”. United have not been relegated since 1974 but find themselves in a battle for survival despite still enjoying one of the biggest revenues in world football. The 34 goals they have conceded in all competitions is the worst defensive record of any team in Europe’s top five leagues this season. items.title: Migration en Afrique de l’ouest : Quinze États adoptent la Déclaration de Dakar
items.description: À l'occasion de la conférence ministérielle sur le processus régional de coopération sur les migrations qui s'est achevée hier, à Dakar, les quinze États d'Afrique de l'Ouest présents ont convenu de renforcer leur collaboration. La Déclaration de Dakar, finalisée au terme des travaux, fixe des engagements communs autour de la gouvernance migratoire. La coopération régionale en matière de migration franchit une nouvelle étape. Initiée par le gouvernement du Sénégal en collaboration avec l’Organisation internationale pour les migrations (Oim), la conférence ministérielle sur le processus régional de coopération migratoire s’est achevée hier à Dakar. Les représentants des quinze États participants ont abouti à la finalisation de la Déclaration de Dakar ainsi qu’à l’élaboration d’une feuille de route pour la période 2027-2028. Ces deux instruments serviront de cadre à une réponse concertée face aux défis migratoires en Afrique de l’Ouest. Présentant les conclusions des deux journées de discussions techniques, Dieynaba Touré Bathily, directrice des Affaires juridiques et consulaires au ministère de l’Intégration africaine, des Affaires étrangères et des Sénégalais de l’extérieur, a indiqué que les travaux ont permis de dégager trois axes de convergence : la gouvernance et la coopération régionale, la protection des migrants et l’accès aux services et les liens entre mobilité, intégration régionale et développement. Selon Mme Bathily, l’adoption de la Déclaration de Dakar permet de formaliser les engagements politiques communs autour de ces priorités. L'enjeu consiste désormais à renforcer la coopération aux frontières et entre les services consulaires, à faciliter la circulation régulière, à garantir la continuité de la protection des migrants et à promouvoir une mobilité professionnelle fondée sur le recrutement équitable et la reconnaissance des compétences. Pour traduire ces engagements en actes, les États ont simultanément adopté une feuille de route prévoyant la désignation de points focaux nationaux, le déploiement d'actions pilotes et la mise en place de mécanismes de suivi sur deux ans. « Ce document précise également des procédures de coopération pour des besoins pratiques, tels que la vérification de documents ou de nationalités, l'organisation du transit des migrants volontaires ou encore la transmission d'alertes liées à la surveillance en mer », a détaillé la directrice des Affaires juridiques et consulaires au ministère de l’Intégration africaine, des Affaires étrangères et des Sénégalais de l’extérieur. Prenant la parole, la directrice générale de l’Oim, Amy Eileen Pope, a insisté sur la nécessité d’une riposte collective face aux réseaux de traite et de trafic de migrants. Évoquant le sort des jeunes et des femmes victimes de fausses promesses d’emploi, elle a rappelé qu’« aucun pays ne peut s'attaquer seul à ces réseaux », plaidant pour une migration mieux organisée, levier d’emploi et de développement économique pour les territoires. Pour sa part, le ministre de la Justice, Garde des Sceaux, Me Moussa Sarr qui présidait la cérémonie au nom de son collègue Cheikh Niang, ministre des Affaires étrangères, a salué l’aboutissement de ce processus engagé depuis plusieurs mois. Rappelant la détermination du Chef de l’État, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, à sévir contre les passeurs, il a mis l'accent sur le volet pénal. « La lutte contre le trafic illicite de migrants et la traite des personnes suppose une entraide judiciaire efficace entre nos États », a-t-il déclaré, tout en réitérant la volonté du Sénégal de faire de la prévention de la migration irrégulière une priorité. Souleymane WANE

items.title: Horror in Calabar: Driver runs over Nursing student twice, flees
items.description: By Emma Una CALABAR—A nursing student of the School of Nursing, Mary Slessor Avenue, Calabar, identified as Cynthia Eni, has been killed after a speeding driver reportedly knocked her down and reversed to run over her a second time before fleeing the scene. The incident, which occurred at the weekend, happened as Cynthia was crossing the road into the school compound after going out with two colleagues to buy some items. A friend of the deceased, Mercy, who witnessed the incident, said the driver first knocked Cynthia down before reversing and running over her again as people attempted to come to her rescue. “It was a bewildering scene. When the car knocked her down, we were shouting for help and before some boys could rush down, the same car returned and climbed her again. When the car was approaching we thought the driver had come to help but was surprised when the car ran over her again.” Mercy said the driver took advantage of the fading light and the fact that people were focused on the victim to escape, adding that the vehicle’s registration number was not visible. She said Cynthia, who was about 30, had completed her Community Health studies at the College of Health Technology and enrolled at the School of Nursing to obtain an additional qualification. “We don’t know what was in the driver’s mind. Even if he was drunk or had some issues with Cynthia, he should have had some sense of humanity and not come back to crush her the way he did.” Mercy said she could not recall any misunderstanding between the deceased and fellow students or outsiders. “We leave everything to God,” she said, breaking down in tears. There was no official at the Provost’s Office available to comment on the incident as it occurred at the weekend. items.title: 52e Championnat du monde de pétanque : Après Singapour, le Burkina Faso terrasse l’Argentine et affirme ses ambitions
items.description: En compétition au 52e Championnat du monde de pétanque à Khon Kaen, en Thaïlande, l'équipe nationale du Burkina Faso confirme sa belle forme internationale. Après une entame de tournoi frustrante face à la Slovaquie, les Étalons boulistes ont réagi avec panache en enchaînant deux victoires probantes, dont une démonstration d'adresse et de maîtrise tactique contre l'Argentine (13-5) ce 22 novembre 2026. Une montée en puissance qui positionne le contingent burkinabè parmi les nations les plus redoutables de ces Mondiaux asiatiques. Les boulodromes de l'Université de Khon Kaen résonnent sous les carreaux burkinabè. Pour leur troisième sortie au 52e Championnat du monde de pétanque organisé par la Fédération Internationale (FIPJP), les Étalons du Burkina Faso ont livré une prestation de haute volée face à une sélection argentine accrocheuse. Maîtres du bouchon et intransigeants au tir de précision, les pointeurs et tireurs burkinabè n'ont laissé aucune chance à l'Albiceleste, s'imposant sur le score sans appel de 13 à 5. Une victoire nette qui confirme l'excellente santé sportive de la discipline au pays des Hommes intègres. Cette montée en puissance est le fruit d'un réajustement tactique rapide et d'un mental d'acier. La compétition avait pourtant débuté sous une note d'amertume avec une courte défaite sur le fil contre la Slovaquie (10-11), où la victoire avait échappé aux Burkinabè dans les ultimes mènes. Loin de se déstabiliser, les Étalons ont immédiatement rectifié le tir lors de leur deuxième confrontation en balayant Singapour sur un score fleuve de 13 à 1. En enchaînant cette deuxième victoire consécutive contre l'Argentine, le Burkina Faso prouve qu'il a tiré les enseignements de son faux pas initial pour imposer son jeu de précision et d'attaque. Régulièrement illustré sur la scène africaine et internationale, le Burkina Faso entend marquer de son empreinte cette édition 2026. Face aux ténors traditionnels de la discipline, le groupe burkinabè s'appuie sur une cohésion d'équipe sans faille et une adresse remarquable au tir. Alors que la phase de poules et les tours à élimination directe se poursuivent en terre thaïlandaise, la dynamique enclenchée par les Étalons suscite un immense espoir auprès des supporters à Ouagadougou et à travers la diaspora. L’article 52e Championnat du monde de pétanque : Après Singapour, le Burkina Faso terrasse l'Argentine et affirme ses ambitions est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Port City FC and Heart of Lions share spoils in goalless draw
items.description: Port City and Heart of Lions settled for a 0-0 draw at Port City’s home in the Ghana Premier League on Sunday, November 22. The two teams battled it out at the Daasebre Boamah Darko II Park in Kukurantumi. Port city entered Matchday 12 aiming to extend their unbeaten streak to six matches. The hosts brought an intimidating home record of 25 consecutive home league matches without a loss stretching back to their Division one league campaign. On Matchday 11, Port City staged a comeback to claim a 3-0 victory over Premier League debutants Debibi United. Meanwhile, Hearts of Lions suffered a 2-1 defeat over Dreams FC following a previous 3-0 loss to Hearts of Oak. After a hard fought goalless first half, both teams pushed hard for a breakthrough after the break. However the score remained 0-0 after 90 minutes, as neither side could break the deadlock. Following a run of poor results, the Lions continue to find themselves16th in the relegation zone with 12 points, leaving them with work to do to turn their season around. Despite the draw , the newly promoted Port City FC still remain 3rd with 22 points, determined to keep up their push as serious title contenders.

items.title: Campagne 30 % à Khossanto : les femmes au cœur des revenus miniers
items.description: Oxfam et ses partenaires plaident pour l’affectation de 30 % du Fonds d’appui au développement local (FADL) aux projets d’autonomisation économique des femmes et à l’éducation des filles dans les zones minières. Cette revendication était au centre d’un dialogue multiacteurs organisé samedi à Khossanto, dans le département de SarayaSaraya. Lancée en 2019, la campagne « 30 % » vise à renforcer les retombées de l’exploitation minière au profit des femmes des communautés impactées. Selon Dalila Dosso, coordonnatrice de la campagne Égalité et Équité d’Oxfam au Sénégal, les échanges avec les populations doivent alimenter un document de politique publique destiné aux institutions, dans le cadre notamment de la révision du Code minier. Présent à la rencontre, le député Babacar Ndiaye, président de la commission énergie et ressources minérales de l’Assemblée nationale, a réaffirmé son engagement à défendre ce plaidoyer. Le maire de Khossanto, Mamady Cissokho, a, pour sa part, indiqué que sur les 208 millions de francs CFA reçus par sa commune au titre du FADL, 86 millions ont été consacrés aux activités génératrices de revenus des femmes et à l’acquisition d’équipements pour alléger leurs travaux. Le directeur de l’ARD de Kédougou, Kalidou Cissokho, a salué cette initiative, tout en appelant à renforcer les capacités des femmes à porter des projets structurants. Il a également plaidé pour une meilleure prise en compte des jeunes garçons, des départements et des personnes vulnérables. Le point focal du FADL, Ousmane Niang, a enfin précisé que les départements, au même titre que les communes, bénéficient des ressources du fonds. Amadou DIOP (Correspondant)

items.title: Incendie à la zone d’activités commerciales et administratives : Des tonnes de marchandises consumées par les flammes
items.description: Le vendredi 20 novembre 2026, le ministre de la Sécurité, Mahamadou Sana est allé constater les dégâts de l’incendie intervenu le jeudi 19 novembre 2026 à la zone d’activités commerciales et administratives (ZACA) sise à l’arrondissement 1 de Ouagadougou. La date du jeudi 19 novembre 2026 restera graver dans les mémoires des commerçants de la zone d’activités commerciales et administratives (ZACA) de Ouagadougou. Pour cause, un incendie intervenu aux environs de 19h. A son passage, il a causé d’énormes dégâts matériels. Des marchandises, des motos, des batteries et d’autres matériaux plastique ont été touchées par les flammes. Ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026, le ministre de la Securité, Mahamadou Sana est allé constater la situation. « Nous sommes venus aujourd’hui nous s’imprégner de la situation réelle sur le terrain. Nous nous sommes rendus compte qu’il ne s’agissait pas des explosifs mais plutôt des matières dangereuses notamment des insecticides surement mal conditionnés ou qui ont été mis dans des conditions favorisant le déclenchement de cet incendie. Les sapeurs-pompiers ont pu intervenir à temps et on a eu que des dégâts matériels, heureusement pas de dégât humaine » a-t-il constaté. Selon lui, le transport de ces produits obéit à certaines règles, que ce soit des bouteilles de gaz, des insecticides. « Il y a des normes strictes à respecter en matière des transports, et quand on les respecte, il va de soi qu’il ait un meilleur transport mais quand on ne le fait pas, ces genres d’incidents interviennent et le moindre incident va causer d’énorme dégât » a -t-il expliqué. A cet effet, il a invité les transporteurs au respect strict de cette règlementation. Séance tenante, le ministre a donné des instructions à son département pour qu’une campagne de sensibilisation soit menée au profit des populations sur le transport des marchandises et la brigade Laabal est mis à contribution pour le contrôle de transport de certaines marchandises dans les marchés et yaars. Synthèse de Fleur BIRBA Sidwaya L’article Incendie à la zone d’activités commerciales et administratives : Des tonnes de marchandises consumées par les flammes est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Bayelsa Boat Mishap: Death toll rises to 29
items.description: …Tinubu approves N250m for victims’ families, directs NDDC to procure boats …FG backs probe of incident …Diri makes case for senatorial roads By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The death toll from last Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with more than 51 survivors recorded, as search and recovery operations continue. President Bola Tinubu has also approved N250 million to support families of the victims and directed the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) to procure boats to improve water transportation in the riverine communities. Vice President Kashim Shettima announced the presidential intervention on Sunday during a condolence visit to Bayelsa State on the President’s directive. The boat, which was conveying passengers to Ukubie community for a burial ceremony, capsized near Oweikorogha community, leaving several persons dead and others rescued. Speaking at the Government House, Yenagoa, after visiting hospitalised survivors at the Bayelsa Medical University Teaching Hospital (BMUTH), Shettima said the President had directed relevant federal agencies to collaborate with the state government in the search and rescue operations and provide support for those affected. He described the incident as a national tragedy, noting that behind the casualty figures were individuals with families, relationships and responsibilities to their communities and society. “Each person involved has a name, an identity, a history, relationships and responsibilities. Family members cannot come to terms with the fact that someone who left home for a funeral will never return,” he said. The Vice President acknowledged the peculiar geographical challenges of Bayelsa, where waterways serve as major transportation routes connecting communities to schools, hospitals, markets and other essential services. “Geography can determine how people travel, but it will never determine the worth of the lives involved,” Shettima stated. He disclosed that Tinubu had directed the NDDC to procure boats to improve transportation in the riverine areas of the state. Shettima also commended Governor Douye Diri for his response to the tragedy and the establishment of a commission of inquiry to investigate the incident. He stressed the need for the recommendations of the panel to be implemented to prevent a recurrence. In his remarks, Diri thanked Tinubu and the Vice President for their intervention and for identifying with the people of Bayelsa at a difficult time. The governor recalled that Shettima was among the first senior government officials to contact him following the incident, alongside the President’s Chief of Staff and the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy. He said the Federal Government’s response demonstrated its commitment to the welfare of Bayelsans, contrasting it with what he described as the inadequate attention the state received during the 2022 flood disaster. “On behalf of the government and people of Bayelsa State, I acknowledge the very sound leadership of Mr President, your humble self and your team for the human face. We cannot thank you enough,” Diri said. Describing the incident as a painful loss, the governor said many of the victims were young people whose futures held great promise. However, he said preliminary findings suggested that the accident might have been avoided if established safety regulations had been observed. “From what we have gathered so far, the boat was not seaworthy or river-worthy. The loading point was not an approved government loading point, and that is why all the necessary government requirements were not found in this incident,” he said. Diri explained that the state government had taken charge of the rescue operation in collaboration with federal agencies, security services and other relevant authorities. He added that the government was also taking responsibility for the medical bills and feeding of survivors receiving treatment in various hospitals across the state. Providing an update on the incident, the governor said 29 persons had been confirmed dead, while more than 51 survivors had been recorded. He said search and recovery operations were ongoing, adding that authorities were yet to retrieve the capsized boat. According to him, the exact casualty figure could only be established after the recovery of the boat, as some bodies might still be trapped inside it. Meanwhile, the governor appealed to the Federal Government to intervene in the slow pace of work on the second phase of the Nembe-Brass Road project, despite its approval by President Tinubu. He explained that Bayelsa’s riverine and deltaic terrain made road construction particularly challenging and expensive, requiring sustained collaboration between the federal and state governments. Diri urged the Vice President to convey the state’s concerns to the President and support efforts to accelerate work on the project, as well as collaborate with the state government on the completion of the three senatorial roads. Shettima also met with families of the victims and presented cash assistance to them. Those present during the visit included the governor’s wife, Dr Gloria Diri; Minority Leader of the House of Representatives, Fred Agbedi; Senators Konbowei Benson and Benson Agadaga; and the member representing Southern Ijaw Federal Constituency, Rodney Ambaiowei. Others were the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Senator Heineken Lokpobiri; Deputy Speaker of the Bayelsa State House of Assembly, Michael Ogbere; former deputy governors Peremobowei Ebebi and Rear Admiral Gboribiogha John-Jonah; and NDDC Managing Director, Dr Samuel Ogbuku. Also present were the Managing Director of the Niger Delta Basin Development Authority, Prince Ebitimi Amgbare; former NDDC Managing Director, Chief Ndutimi Alaibe; Chief David Lyon; and PANDEF National Chairman, Dr Boladei Igali. The Director-General of the National Emergency Management Agency, Mrs Zubaida Abubakar Umar, was also part of the Vice President’s entourage. items.title: Niger : le MISPAT met les données au cœur de la décision avec son Comité Statistique…
items.description: Le Ministère de l’Intérieur, de la Sécurité Publique et de l’Administration du Territoire (MISPAT) a lancé, le vendredi 20 novembre 2026 à Niamey, les travaux de son Comité Statistique, au lendemain de son installation officielle. Une initiative qui traduit la volonté du département de placer les données fiables au service de la planification, du suivi et de la prise de décision. La cérémonie d’ouverture a été présidée par le Secrétaire Général Adjoint du Ministère, M. Abdoul Kader Garba Moussa. Il était entouré de M. Goumey Hama, Directeur de la Statistique et Vice-Président du comité, ainsi que de M. Mahamadou Salha Achoura, représentant de l’Institut National de la Statistique (INS). Des représentants des directions centrales et transversales du Ministère ont également pris part aux travaux. Au nom du Ministre d’État, le Secrétaire Général Adjoint a rappelé que la statistique constitue un instrument essentiel pour éclairer les décisions, orienter les politiques publiques et mesurer les résultats de l’action de l’État. Selon lui, le nouveau comité doit permettre au MISPAT de disposer d’informations crédibles, utiles et directement exploitables par les décideurs. Le Comité Statistique aura notamment pour mission d’harmoniser les outils et méthodes de collecte des données, d’améliorer leur qualité et leur sécurité, et de renforcer la coordination entre les différents services du Ministère. Il devra également bénéficier de l’appui technique de l’Institut National de la Statistique dans l’accomplissement de ses missions. Prenant la parole à cette occasion, le Directeur de la Statistique, M. Goumey Hama, a insisté sur la crédibilité des données mises à la disposition des décideurs. Selon lui, c’est avec des données de qualité que l’on peut anticiper les défis, orienter les interventions et bâtir un meilleur avenir. La création de ce Comité Statistique s’inscrit dans la volonté du Ministère de moderniser ses outils de gestion et de renforcer l’efficacité de l’action publique. En s’appuyant sur des données fiables, le MISPAT entend mieux anticiper les besoins des populations, améliorer le suivi de ses interventions et renforcer la redevabilité de ses services. Les travaux de cette première réunion ont permis aux participants d’échanger sur les priorités du comité, les défis liés à la production des statistiques et les perspectives de collaboration avec l’Institut National de la Statistique. Les échanges ont également mis en lumière la nécessité de disposer de données actualisées, cohérentes et accessibles pour accompagner les réformes en cours. À l’issue de la rencontre, les membres du comité se sont engagés à œuvrer pour la mise en place d’un système statistique ministériel plus performant. L’enjeu est désormais de traduire ces ambitions en actions concrètes, afin que chaque donnée produite contribue efficacement à la prise de décision et à l’amélioration des services rendus aux populations. En déclarant ouverts les travaux, M. Abdoul Kader Garba Moussa a appelé les membres du comité à faire preuve d’engagement, de rigueur et d’esprit de collaboration. L’ambition est claire : faire de chaque chiffre produit par le Ministère un véritable outil au service de la décision publique. items.title: Entretien périodique de l’axe Pâ-Dano-Diébougou : Le ministre Mikaïlou Sidibé constate des imperfections et exige une rigueur absolue
items.description: En route ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026 pour le lancement des travaux du tronçon Batié-Kpuéré-frontière Côte d'Ivoire sur la RN11, le ministre de la Construction de la Patrie, le camarade Mikaïlou Sidibé, a effectué plusieurs arrêts d'inspection sur le chantier d'entretien périodique de la RN12, reliant Pâ, Dano et Diébougou. Confronté à des zones de dégradations précoces causées par des défauts de portance de la chaussée, le ministre, accompagné du conseiller spécial du président du Faso, Roland Somda, a rassuré les usagers : l’ensemble des imperfections sera impérativement traité par l'entreprise adjudicataire avant toute réception des travaux. L'exigence de qualité dans la réalisation des infrastructures publiques ne tolère aucun compromis. Ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026, alors qu'il se rendait au lancement du chantier de construction et de bitumage du tronçon Batié-Kpuéré-frontière Côte d'Ivoire sur la RN11, le ministre de la Construction de la Patrie, le camarade Mikaïlou Sidibé, a marqué plusieurs arrêts le long de la RN12. Accompagné du ministre conseiller spécial du président du Faso chargé de la construction, le camarade Roland Somda, et de ses collaborateurs techniques, le ministre a tenu à observer directement l’état d’avancement et la conformité des travaux en cours sur la section Pâ–Dano–Diébougou. Les interventions menées sur la RN12 s’inscrivent dans un programme spécifique d'entretien périodique. Le projet consiste en un resurfaçage de la chaussée au moyen d'un enrobé bitumineux de 5 cm d'épaisseur, et non d'une réhabilitation lourde globale. Le chantier comprend également le traitement structurant des traversées d'agglomération au niveau de Pâ, Founzan, Dano, Djikologo et Diébougou. Dans ces localités, les aménagements prévoient notamment l'élargissement à 2×2 voies à Dano, ainsi que des travaux d'assainissement et d’éclairage public destinés à sécuriser et moderniser le cadre de vie riverain. Au cours de l'inspection, la délégation ministérielle a arrêté son attention sur plusieurs zones présentant des dégradations anormales. Le ministre Mikaïlou Sidibé a expliqué que ces désordres proviennent d'une portance de la chaussée qui n'était pas uniforme sur l'ensemble du tronçon. Soucieux de préserver la durabilité de l'ouvrage, le ministre a affirmé que ces défaillances ont été clairement répertoriées et que l'entreprise exécutante apportera les traitements nécessaires pour corriger l'ensemble des imperfections constatées avant toute réception officielle des travaux. Réitérant la détermination de son département à veiller au respect strict des normes de qualité, le ministre a tenu à rassurer les usagers sur la livraison finale d'une route conforme aux exigences requises. items.title: ACPN petitions AGF over Edo drug enforcement, alleges regulatory overreach
items.description: By Chioma Obinna The Association of Community Pharmacists of Nigeria (ACPN) on Sunday petitioned the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, over alleged regulatory overreach and unlawful pharmaceutical enforcement by the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee. The association urged the Federal Government to intervene, warning that state agencies must not assume regulatory powers vested in federal institutions under existing laws. In a petition titled “Exercising Regulatory Control within the Constitutional Framework in Nigeria”, and jointly signed by ACPN National Chairman, Pharm. Ambrose Igwekamma Ezeh, and National Secretary, Pharm. Obiageri Ikwu, ACPN said it supported efforts to rid the country of counterfeit, adulterated, substandard and expired medicines but insisted that such interventions must be evidence-based, follow due process and comply with the relevant laws. The association specifically faulted the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee for reportedly declaring Camosunate a banned medicinal product in Nigeria, arguing that the committee lacked the statutory authority to make such a pronouncement. According to ACPN, “The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) is empowered by law to register, ban or deregister drugs and food products in the country. A verification of NAFDAC’s official Green Book showed that Camosunate Children Powder, with registration number 04-7908, manufactured by Front Pharmaceuticals PLC and marketed by Geneith Pharmaceuticals Limited, remained an active registered medicinal product.” The association said the product’s registration was approved on November 26, 2025, and would remain valid until November 25, 2030. “This is an official regulatory record, not an opinion or an industry rumour. There was no official NAFDAC declaration, suspension, withdrawal or cancellation notice establishing that the specific Camosunate formulation pronounced banned by the Edo committee was prohibited in Nigeria.” The association also raised concerns over a reported enforcement operation involving ALSO CARE Pharmacy in Evbuodia community, along Airport Road, Benin City, and the public allegations made against the establishment. It called for the disclosure of the products seized, their registration particulars and the independent regulatory evidence supporting any allegation of counterfeit or prohibited medicines. “No pharmacy should be publicly condemned on the basis of unverified assertions,” the association said. Citing the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (Establishment) Act 2022, ACPN maintained that the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) had statutory responsibility for the registration, inspection, licensing and regulation of pharmaceutical premises across the country. It specifically referenced Sections 4, 22, 31 and 32 of the Act, arguing that pharmaceutical premises regulation must be undertaken by legally designated authorities. The association also cited Sections 7 and 8 of the Counterfeit and Fake Drugs and Unwholesome Processed Foods (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, Cap C34 LFN 2004, which provide for the constitution and powers of state task forces. It, however, argued that such provisions did not automatically empower state consumer protection committees to assume specialised pharmaceutical regulatory functions. “Such powers cannot automatically be appropriated by State Consumer Protection Committee, as it is not recognised to carry out such functions in all the relevant existing federal laws,” it said. ACPN further cited Section 5 of the NAFDAC Act, Cap N1 LFN 2004, as the statutory basis for NAFDAC’s responsibility for regulating medicinal products. The association urged Fagbemi to liaise with Attorneys-General and Commissioners for Justice in the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory to sensitise government agencies on their constitutional and statutory responsibilities. It also called for an end to pharmaceutical enforcement activities conducted without appropriate legal authority and urged all relevant agencies to respect the mandates of NAFDAC and PCN. While reaffirming its commitment to protecting Nigerians from fake and falsified medicines, the association warned against the misuse of consumer protection powers. “Consumer protection must never become a licence for misinformation, administrative arbitrariness, or regulatory intimidation. Public officials must be accountable for their claims.” The post ACPN petitions AGF over Edo drug enforcement, alleges regulatory overreach appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Musique : Freddy Traoré met sur le marché son premier album de 8 titres
items.description: L'artiste burkinabè Freddy Traoré a officiellement présenté son nouvel album, le samedi 21 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Intitulée « La vérité est la force de la paix », cette œuvre de huit titres, interprétés en français et en dioula, vise à contribuer à la mobilisation et à la conscientisation des peuples du Sahel et d'Afrique autour des idéaux panafricains. Avec cet opus, Freddy Traoré signe son premier album et y véhicule des valeurs de vérité, de patriotisme, d'intégrité et d'engagement dans la lutte pour la souveraineté africaine, portée notamment par le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré et ses pairs de l'Alliance des États du Sahel (AES). Freddy Traoré, appelle les peuples a mutualisé les efforts contre l'impérialisme L'artiste lance également un appel aux peuples burkinabè et de l'AES afin qu'ils restent engagés et vigilants face aux défis de cette lutte. Pour lui, il est essentiel de cultiver la vérité, le patriotisme et l'intégrité pour préserver les acquis revendiqués dans cette dynamique de reconquête de la dignité et de la liberté des peuples africains. « Il ne faut pas que nous nous trahissions pour perdre cela », insiste-t-il, invitant les Africains à rester unis, véridiques et dignes dans leur engagement. Selon son approche, la lutte panafricaine est avant tout celle des hommes et des femmes africains pour leur liberté. Elle vise à empêcher un retour aux systèmes d'exploitation, de domination et d'impérialisme colonial. Face à la presse, Freddy Traoré a estimé que la reconquête de la souveraineté et de la dignité africaines doit nécessairement s'accompagner d'une responsabilité collective. À travers ses huit titres, proposés en français et en dioula, l'artiste souhaite faire de la musique un instrument de sensibilisation et de mobilisation en faveur de la cause panafricaine. Son message central est un appel à la solidarité, à l'intégrité et à la vigilance, afin d'éviter toute forme de trahison susceptible de compromettre les aspirations d'émancipation des peuples africains. Notons que l'album est disponible en clé USB au prix unitaire de 10 000 F CFA, avec une vidéo intégrée. items.title: EFEDCOM elects Dr Yacouba Diarra as President
items.description: The ECOWAS Federation of Chambers of Mines (EFEDCOM) has elected Dr Yacouba Diarra as its new President. He has pledged to champion investment-friendly mining policies, strengthen regional cooperation and promote sustainable mining across West Africa. Dr Diarra, who also serves as President of the Professional Association of Miners of Côte d’Ivoire (GPMCI), succeeds Mr Adama Soro. He took office at the Federation’s 7th Annual General Meeting, held on 17 November 2026 at the Radisson Blu Hotel in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire. In his acceptance address, Dr Diarra called for closer collaboration between governments and the mining industry to develop consistent and predictable policies that support long-term investment. He pledged to strengthen EFEDCOM’s engagement with national governments and ECOWAS institutions so that industry perspectives are reflected in regional policy decisions. “Our ambition is to make EFEDCOM a strong, influential and unifying organisation, capable of effectively defending the interests of the mining industry and contributing to the economic development of the ECOWAS region,” he said. Dr Diarra also outlined plans to deepen cooperation among national chambers of mines through information sharing, technical collaboration and the development of common positions on issues affecting the industry. He stressed that mining growth must deliver tangible benefits for host countries and communities. He identified local content development, skills training, knowledge transfer, environmental protection and community development as priorities. Dr Diarra noted that he was taking office at a time of significant growth in Côte d’Ivoire’s mining sector, marked by the development of major mines and discoveries of gold and other critical minerals. About Dr Yacouba Diarra Dr Diarra is a mining engineer with more than 20 years of experience in the sector and is regarded as one of the pioneers of mineral exploration in Côte d’Ivoire. He holds a doctorate in Economic Geology and Mining Environment from the National Polytechnic Institute Félix Houphouët-Boigny in Yamoussoukro and is a graduate of the Centre for Advanced Studies in Mining Administration at the École Nationale des Mines de Paris. He received the 2022 Good Governance Award for Best Manager in Côte d’Ivoire’s Mining Sector and has served as President of GPMCI since February 2025.

items.title: Emir of Daura: Lawyer demands police probe
items.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — Abuja-based legal practitioner, Pelumi Olajengbesi, has called on the Nigeria Police Force to immediately commence an independent investigation into the allegation of sexual assault levelled against the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, by a foreign tourist. Olajengbesi described the allegation as disturbing, stressing that it should not be treated lightly and that all parties must be accorded fairness and due process. He urged the police to investigate the matter thoroughly and independently to establish the facts and ensure that justice was served in accordance with the law. “We must be able to show to the entire world that Nigeria doesn’t condone sexual harassment. Therefore, all parties must be accorded fairness and due process in the interest of justice,” he said. “Sexual harassment has no place in our society. This is a no, no, no for Nigeria!” he declared. The lawyer’s call follows allegations made by a foreign tourist, identified as Mirka on Instagram, where she uses the handle @beduinqa, who accused the Emir of sexually assaulting her during a visit to his palace on November 14. The tourist, who said she was on a 30-day tour of Nigeria, alleged that the traditional ruler held her hand, hugged and kissed her on the cheek before touching her breasts despite her repeated objections. “I told him ‘emir no, no, no, no’ ‘emir you cannot be touching’, but he was just laughing about it,” she wrote. She claimed to have recorded the encounter with Meta smart glasses but waited until she had left Nigeria before making the allegation public. The tourist said the alleged incident was particularly distressing because she had not experienced sexual assault while visiting other parts of the country. “I wasn’t sexually assaulted at any moment when walking through streets of Nigeria, even in busy crowded places, but to my shock, I was assaulted in a palace by a traditional leader who should be behaving in exemplary and dignified way,” she said. The video and her account have since circulated widely on social media platforms, including X, Instagram and Facebook, triggering discussions about consent, the conduct of traditional institutions and accountability. Amnesty International Nigeria has also called on the Katsina State Government and the police to conduct a transparent and independent investigation into the allegation and ensure accountability if it is established. As of Sunday, neither the Daura Emirate Council nor the Katsina State Government had issued an official response to the allegation. The allegation remains unverified, and no finding of wrongdoing has been established against the Emir. The post Emir of Daura: Lawyer demands police probe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ouagadougou-Libreville : Air Burkina renoue avec le ciel gabonais
items.description: La compagnie aérienne nationale Air Burkina a officiellement repris, le samedi 21 novembre 2026, sa liaison aérienne entre Ouagadougou et Libreville, via Cotonou. Le vol 2J591, qui a marqué cette reprise, avait à son bord une délégation burkinabè conduite par le Conseiller technique du Ministre d’Etat, Ministre de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité, le Camarade Jean Victorien TOE. Cette relance renforce les possibilités de mobilité entre les deux pays et ouvre de nouvelles perspectives pour les échanges économiques et la coopération régionale. La cérémonie officielle d’accueil du vol inaugural s’est déroulée à l’Aéroport International Léon-Mba de Libreville, en présence du Secrétaire Général du ministère gabonais des Affaires étrangères, de diplomates du Mali, du Niger, du Togo, du Bénin et du Sénégal, ainsi que des autorités aéroportuaires et de partenaires institutionnels. La délégation burkinabè comprenait également le Président du Conseil d’administration de Air Burkina, le Camarade Dr Drissa SAWADOGO et le Directeur Général de la compagnie, le Camarade Wendkuni Serge Frédéric ZOMBRE. Au nom du Ministre d’Etat, Ministre de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité, le Conseiller technique, le Camarade Jean Victorien TOE, a salué une reprise qui constitue un levier important pour la mobilité des personnes, le développement économique et l’intégration africaine. Il y voit également une nouvelle étape dans le raffermissement des relations entre le Burkina Faso et le Gabon. « La reprise de cette liaison directe entre le Burkina Faso et la République du Gabon marque une nouvelle étape de notre excellente relation d’amitié, de fraternité et de solidarité qui unissent nos deux nations », a-t-il soutenu. Le Conseiller technique du Ministre d’Etat, le Camarade Jean Victorien TOE, a, en outre, exprimé la reconnaissance du Gouvernement burkinabè aux autorités gabonaises pour leur disponibilité et leur engagement en faveur du renforcement des échanges bilatéraux. Pour le Directeur Général de Air Burkina, le Camarade Wendkuni Serge Frédéric ZOMBRE, cette reprise traduit la volonté de la compagnie nationale de consolider son réseau et de faciliter les déplacements entre les peuples africains. « A travers son réseau, notre compagnie entend poursuivre sa mission de rapprochement des peuples, de facilitation de la mobilité et de renforcement des échanges entre les nations africaines », a-t-il déclaré. Le Camarade Wendkuni Serge Frédéric ZOMBRE, a, par ailleurs, réitéré l’engagement de Air Burkina à assurer la régularité et la pérennité de cette desserte, dans le respect des exigences de sécurité, de ponctualité, de régularité et de qualité du service. Il a également salué les connexions aériennes entretenues avec plusieurs pays de la sous-région, notamment le Mali, le Sénégal, le Togo, le Bénin et le Niger. L’Ambassadeur du Burkina Faso au Gabon, le Camarade Issa BORO, a, pour sa part, inscrit cette reprise dans la dynamique de renforcement de la coopération bilatérale. Il a notamment rappelé l’ouverture, en 2026, d’une Ambassade résidente du Gabon à Ouagadougou, ainsi que la tenue de la réunion des experts préparatoire à la deuxième session de la Grande commission mixte de coopération entre les deux pays. « Les travaux de cette réunion ont abouti à l’élaboration d’une vingtaine de projets d’accord qui seront validés ultérieurement par la réunion ministérielle », a-t- il précisé. Avec deux vols par semaine via Cotonou, la reprise de la liaison Ouagadougou-Libreville vient ainsi renforcer la connectivité aérienne entre l’Afrique de l’Ouest et l’Afrique centrale. Elle offre de nouvelles possibilités de déplacement aux voyageurs et contribue à faciliter les échanges entre le Burkina Faso et le Gabon.
