items.title: Diplomatie : Faure Gnassingbé participe à un sommet quadripartite sur les enjeux régionaux au Congo
items.description: Lomé, 22 nov. (ATOP) – Le Président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé, prend part, le dimanche 22 novembre à Oyo, en République du Congo, à un sommet quadripartite consacré au dialogue et à la concertation sur les enjeux régionaux, notamment la situation sécuritaire dans la région des Grands Lacs. Initiée par le président congolais, Denis Sassou N’Guesso, cette rencontre réunit également les dirigeants du Kenya, William Ruto et de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), Félix Tshisékédi. Elle vise à renforcer le dialogue politique et diplomatique entre les pays participants et à promouvoir des solutions concertées face aux tensions susceptibles d’affecter la paix, la stabilité et la coopération régionale. La participation du Président du Conseil togolais s’inscrit dans le cadre de son engagement en faveur du règlement pacifique des conflits et de la consolidation de la paix sur le continent africain. Elle intervient également dans le contexte de sa mission de médiateur désigné par l’Union africaine (UA) dans la crise qui sévit dans l’Est de la RDC. À ce titre, Faure Gnassingbé accompagne les initiatives diplomatiques visant à favoriser une issue pacifique à cette crise et à préserver la stabilité dans la région des Grands Lacs. À travers cette concertation, les dirigeants entendent privilégier le dialogue, la solidarité africaine et la diplomatie préventive face aux défis sécuritaires et politiques du continent. ATOP/JK (Source : communiqué de la Présidence du Conseil)

items.title: Alia, Akume, Suswam, others meet over Benue APC crisis
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Governor Hyacinth Alia of Benue State has reiterated his commitment to reconciliation and unity within the All Progressives Congress (APC) following a meeting with prominent party stakeholders in Abuja. The meeting, held on Saturday, November 21, 2026, was convened by the North Central Presidential Reconciliation Committee, chaired by former Katsina State Governor, Senator Ibrahim Shema, as part of efforts to resolve disagreements among party leaders in Benue. Those in attendance included the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume; former Benue State Governor, Senator Gabriel Suswam; Senator Barnabas Gemade; Senator Jack Gyado; and Elder Simon Shango. Alia disclosed the meeting in a post on his verified social media handle, saying the engagement lasted about two hours and provided an opportunity for the stakeholders to discuss the future of the party in the state. He said: “Today, (Saturday, November 21, 2026) I joined fellow Benue APC stakeholders in Abuja for a reconciliation meeting convened by the North Central Presidential Reconciliation Committee, chaired by Sen. Ibrahim Shehu Shema, former Governor of Katsina State. “The meeting, which lasted about two hours, brought together the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Sen. George Akume, former Benue State Governor, Sen. Gabriel Suswam, Sen. Barnabas Gemade, Sen. Jack Gyado and Elder Simon Shango. “I thank Sen. Shema and his committee for bringing us together. Reconciliation takes a willingness to listen, to speak frankly and to keep working together even where differences remain. “My commitment is clear. I will continue to engage with our leaders and stakeholders in the interest of a united APC, while keeping the peace, security and development of Benue State at the centre of my work. “The people of Benue entrusted us with the responsibility to serve, and that responsibility must continue to guide us.” The post Alia, Akume, Suswam, others meet over Benue APC crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tinubu approves ₦1.5tr recapitalisation of BoA, says APC-PCC
items.description: ….Commits ₦450b to farm financing By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC on Sunday said President Bola Tinubu has approved a ₦1.5 trillion recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture BoA and committed ₦450 billion to agricultural financing programmes. The council said the commitment is meant “to strengthen food security, expand domestic production, and improve the productivity of smallholder farmers across the country, especially in Northern Nigeria.” In a statement issued by its Spokesperson, Dele Alake, the council said the bank had reached “over 500,000 smallholder farmers.” It added that the President “also approved a ₦1.5 trillion recapitalisation to expand agricultural financing and support the cultivation of 500,000 hectares under the Renewed Hope Agenda.” According to the statement, the Federal Government “went beyond providing farmers with loans; it also addressed access to quality seeds, fertiliser, mechanisation, irrigation, storage facilities, commodity markets, and other essential components of the agricultural value chain.” On the recapitalisation, the council said it was “a major campaign promise of the President in 2023.” It said the move was designed “to enhance the bank’s financial capacity and ability to provide more affordable and accessible funding to farmers, agricultural cooperatives, processors, aggregators, and other businesses operating across the agricultural value chain.” The statement added: “Under President Tinubu, a stronger Bank of Agriculture would be better positioned to support large-scale agricultural investments, expand its reach to underserved farming communities, and mobilise additional resources for domestic food production.” The council disclosed that the Renewed Hope Smallholder Support and Value Chain Fund, which has a programme value of ₦250 billion, finances farmers through Farmer Aggregation Companies. These companies, it said, “coordinate farmer registration, input distribution, extension services, and market linkages.” The programme, according to the statement, has reached more than 500,000 smallholder farmers across 16 states, including over 70,000 women. It has also supported the distribution of approximately 2.5 million bags of fertiliser and 300,000 bags of certified seeds. The council said the programme targets two million farmers and the distribution of more than 10 million bags of fertiliser. It named Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Niger, Borno, Gombe, Taraba, Adamawa, Yobe and Bauchi among the states receiving attention under the scheme. To shield farmers from price shocks, the statement said, the bank is implementing a ₦200 billion Guaranteed Minimum Price Programme. Under it, the bank “has procured approximately 170,000 metric tonnes of maize, rice, sorghum, and cassava to strengthen commodity markets and protect farmers against distress sales.” The council also said the bank created an Onion Financing Programme in partnership with the National Onion Producers, Processors and Marketers Association of Nigeria (NOPPMAN), which “represents over 11,800 onion farmers.” The scheme provides onion farmers with improved seeds and fertiliser, supports processors with commodity purchase funds, and helps develop storage and solar-powered cooling facilities to cut post-harvest losses. “Under the arrangement, cooperatives will contribute 30 per cent of their input costs, while BOA will finance the remaining 70 per cent,” the statement said. On dry-season farming, it said the bank is working with the All-Farmers Association of Nigeria “to develop a pipeline targeting 400,000 farmers for the 2026 farming cycle.” The initiative covers financing for 120,000 hectares of wheat and another 300,000 hectares for crops including rice, maize, sorghum, millet, cassava and soybeans. The council added that the Nigeria Ginger Recovery Programme has supported 3,200 farmers in Kachia, Kaduna State, with blight-free seeds. It said more than 9,000 bags have been recovered for multiplication, with an expansion planned across 20,000 hectares in 16 states. For women, the bank is “targeting at least 50,000 women nationwide through insured cooperative production financing at nine per cent, in partnership with the Federal Ministries of Women Affairs and Agriculture.” On mechanisation, the statement said 1,571 tractors have been deployed to 23 states under the Renewed Hope National Agricultural Mechanisation Programme. They are expected to mechanise 1.2 million hectares of farmland. It also cited a ₦385 billion productive-use-of-electricity programme, which “provides 44,000 electric cargo tricycles and 100,000 solar irrigation pumps, targeting 500,000 farming families.” “The interventions demonstrated President Tinubu’s commitment to transforming agriculture into a major driver of economic growth, food security, and job creation”, the council added. The post Tinubu approves ₦1.5tr recapitalisation of BoA, says APC-PCC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NDC dismisses allegations of hoarding ₦6bn campaign funds
items.description: Party says money is reserved for operations, accuses critics of seeking access to development fund By Henry Umoru ABUJA – The national leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has dismissed allegations that it is withholding more than ₦6 billion meant for its presidential campaign, describing the claims as false and misleading. The party said the allegations reflected a lack of understanding of party administration and the funding requirements of political campaigns. Some members of the NDC National Campaign Council (NCC) had reportedly accused the party’s national leadership of failing to release adequate funds for campaign activities, including grassroots mobilisation, billboard advertisements and the printing of posters. The aggrieved members alleged that more than ₦6 billion realised from the sale of nomination forms and contributions by aspirants had been kept in a fixed deposit account while the campaign council struggled to finance basic activities. They also claimed that 75 per cent of the money came from the South-East, following the entry of aspirants who joined the party alongside its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and expressed concern that the alleged funding constraints could affect his electoral prospects. However, speaking with Vanguard, the party’s National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, dismissed the allegations as rumours allegedly being promoted by individuals seeking to create divisions within the party. He said the claims were intended to create friction between Obi and the party’s national leadership. “These are rumours and machinations of mischief makers who don’t wish the party well, and want to create problems where there is none between our presidential candidate and the national leader of our party. “Also, it shows acute ignorance on the part of those peddling the rumours about party administration and how presidential campaigns are funded,” he said. Director advised those making the allegations to familiarise themselves with party administration and the provisions of the Electoral Act on campaign financing. However, a senior party source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, confirmed that the campaign council had yet to receive substantial funding from the national leadership, despite the revenue reportedly generated from the sale of nomination forms. The source expressed concern that the funding situation could hamper publicity, grassroots mobilisation and other campaign activities. According to the source, the party disclosed at its third National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting that it had generated about ₦8 billion, spent approximately ₦2 billion and retained about ₦6 billion in a fixed deposit account. The source said the funds were generated through the sale of nomination forms and development levies. “Let me also inform you that more than 80 per cent of the candidates could not pay for the nomination and expression of interest forms. They were given forms free. Many states still do not have offices, and the party is assisting them. The national leadership recently got its office. “The Obidient Movement is coming out crying about money. Where are the funds for senatorial, governorship and other positions?” the source queried. The source further disclosed that the party had proposed the establishment of a National Campaign Fund involving its presidential candidate, his running mate, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, and the national leadership. According to the source, the arrangement proposed the allocation of ₦1 billion to the South-South, another ₦1 billion to the South-East, while the remaining ₦3 billion would be managed by the Campaign Council. The source claimed that Obi was asked to contribute ₦5 billion towards establishing the fund but provided only ₦220 million, out of which ₦200 million was subsequently transferred to the National Campaign Council. “The party is not holding any campaign money,” the source insisted. The source further alleged that those demanding access to the money were seeking the release of funds contributed for the party’s development. “They want the development fund money people paid to be given to them. The ₦6 billion is to run the party. Only Aisha Yusuf has helped to open an account to assist the party. The party has not raised funds, Obi has not raised funds. “The party will be going to Edo State on Wednesday. The party has no money; the people of Edo State will finance the visit. “If we give them the money we saved to run the election, we will not have money to run the party,” the source said. The source also lamented the absence of adequate funding for campaign publicity, including posters, billboards and youth mobilisation, as well as activities involving various support groups. Vanguard’s efforts to obtain the reaction of the National Campaign Council spokesperson, Dr Constance Ikokwu, were unsuccessful, as she did not respond to a WhatsApp message sent to her over a period of more than five hours. Recall that the NDC, at its third NEC meeting held on October 24 at JD Event Centre, Abuja, announced that it had generated ₦8,529,632,438.77 in revenue since its establishment seven months earlier. The party attributed the revenue to the sale of nomination forms, contributions from supporters, membership dues and levies. Presenting the financial statement, the National Treasurer, Dr Peter Onigah, said the party had spent approximately ₦2.40 billion and retained a balance of about ₦6.13 billion. He said the expenditure covered party activities, including primaries, publicity, salaries and other administrative expenses. Onigah said the party had maintained financial discipline and ensured that resources entrusted to its leadership were managed prudently. He explained that its financial management was guided by the experience of party officials, advice from national leaders and the National Working Committee (NWC). According to him, the party would provide a detailed breakdown of its financial transactions as it approached the end of its first accounting year. “We have been very prudent. Our chief is made up of technocrats, people who are experienced and people who have different capacities,” he said. Onigah also appealed to Nigerians and party members to support the party financially, noting that it was still developing its structures and had yet to control government at any level. “As a new party, we don’t have people in government yet. All of us are outside the government. So we need to contribute together and ensure that our party will prevail and achieve the desired objectives,” he said. items.title: I didn’t politicise it — Gov Yusuf narrates how wife left Kano Govt House
items.description: Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, has broken his silence on his marital crisis with wife, Zainab, recounting how she allegedly left the Government House and later initiated divorce proceedings against him in Abuja. The governor, in an interview with BBC Hausa aired on Sunday, said he had remained quiet despite developments in the marriage, which he said had lasted about two decades and produced children. Yusuf said Zainab, a niece of his former political ally, Rabiu Kwankwaso, was previously married before they got together. He recalled that their relationship eventually deteriorated, leading to her departure from the Government House, an experience he said he endured without publicly discussing the matter. “Many things happened, to the point where her belongings were packed and she was taken away from my house, and through it all, I remained patient and did not speak out,” Yusuf said. He said he had tried to reassure their children that their mother would return, but was subsequently taken aback when the matter ended up in court. The governor said he was particularly surprised that the divorce suit was filed in Abuja rather than Kano. “Suddenly, she dragged me to court, a court in Abuja, not even in Kano,” he said. Yusuf described the development as distressing, adding that he had information about the circumstances surrounding his wife’s departure but would not publicly disclose the details. Asked whether he was using the family dispute for political purposes, the governor denied bringing politics into the matter, questioning how anyone in a similar situation would react. “I am not the one who politicised it. If this was done to you, how would you feel?” he asked. He further lamented that his wife’s belongings were removed and she was taken to another residence without his knowledge, before he learnt that she had instituted legal proceedings against him. The marital dispute is before the Upper Area Court in the Gudu District of Abuja, where the divorce case, marked CV/97/26, was adjourned until December 15. The adjournment followed a request by Kano Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature, who represented Yusuf, for more time to brief the governor on the court proceedings. The crisis has drawn political attention because of Yusuf’s relationship with Kwankwaso, who played a significant role in his political rise. Their relationship reportedly deteriorated after Yusuf defected from the New Nigeria Peoples Party to the All Progressives Congress in January 2026, while Kwankwaso later joined the New Nigeria Democratic Congress. The post I didn’t politicise it — Gov Yusuf narrates how wife left Kano Govt House appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: L’armée malienne annonce avoir neutralisé des hommes armés et détruit du matériel dans près de Kidal
items.description: L'armée malienne a annoncé samedi avoir neutralisé quatre hommes armés et détruit un véhicule au nord-est de la ville de Niounou. Dans un communiqué, l’armée a indiqué que ses forces avaient repéré des hommes armés se déplaçant à moto et en véhicule au nord-est de Niounou, précisant qu’une frappe visant deux motos avait permis de neutraliser quatre hommes armés, avant qu’une autre frappe ne détruise une camionnette. Il a ajouté que ses forces avaient pris pour cible, mercredi dernier, un lieu de rassemblement d’hommes armés situé à 119 kilomètres au sud-ouest de Kidal, après y avoir repéré des individus, du matériel militaire et des véhicules, sur la base de renseignements précis. Le communiqué a indiqué que d’autres frappes avaient visé, vendredi, des positions d’hommes armés situées à 78 kilomètres à l’est de Kidal, qui abritaient des individus, du matériel militaire et des ravitaillements logistiques. Ces opérations s’inscrivent dans le cadre de l’opération « Dougoukoloko » menée par l’armée malienne pour contrôler et sécuriser son territoire.

items.title: L'Égypte, le Soudan et l'Érythrée rejettent le rôle des milices armées au Soudan et leur armement depuis l’étranger
items.description: Une reunion trilaterale entre le ministre egyptien des Affaires etrangeres, Badr Abdelatty, et ses homologues soudanais, Mohi El-Din Salem, et erythreen, Osman Saleh, s'est tenue le 21 novembre, en marge du sixieme Forum d'Assouan pour la paix et le developpement durable. Reaffirmant les liens historiques entre leurs pays, les trois ministres se sont engages a renforcer la consultation et la coordination sur les questions d'interet commun, dans le but de soutenir la securite et la stabilite regionales et de servir les interets communs de leurs peuples, selon un communique publie par le ministere egyptien des Affaires etrangeres. Responsabilite securitaire en mer Rouge et rejet du role des groupes armes L'evolution de la situation regionale figurait parmi les axes des discussions. Les trois chefs de diplomatie ont souligne l'importance de maintenir la securite et la stabilite en mer Rouge et de garantir la liberte de navigation et la securite des voies maritimes internationales. Les ministres ont par ailleurs souligne que les pays riverains assumaient la responsabilite de la gouvernance de la securite de la mer Rouge, ainsi que celle de la navigation et des voies maritimes mondiales. Les participants a la reunion ont egalement appele a respecter la souverainete, l'unite et l'integrite territoriale du Soudan , ainsi qu'a la preservation de ses institutions nationales, ont rejete, dans la foulee, le role des milices armees et leur approvisionnement en armes depuis l'etranger. Soutien a la souverainete et rejet des mesures unilaterales en matiere de securite et d'eau Les diplomaties egyptienne, erythreenne et soudanaise ont reaffirme leur soutien a l'unite, a la souverainete et a l'integrite territoriale de la Somalie , et se sont prononcees contre la creation d'entites paralleles, reaffirmant egalement leur soutien a l'unite, a la souverainete et a l'integrite territoriale de l'erythree. Dans un autre registre, ils ont rejete les mesures unilaterales concernant la securite et les questions liees a l'eau, soulignant que la consultation entre les trois pays devait renforcer la non-ingerence dans les affaires interieures, le respect de la souverainete des etats et la poursuite de la coordination afin de promouvoir la stabilite et le developpement regionaux. Un accord de formation et de renforcement des capacites signe entre l'egypte et le Soudan Badr Abdelatty et Mohi El-Din Salem ont signe un protocole d'accord distinct entre l'Agence egyptienne de partenariat pour le developpement (EAPD) et le ministere soudanais des Affaires etrangeres et de la Cooperation internationale, en marge du forum, portant sur le renforcement de la cooperation dans les domaines de formation, de qualification professionnelle et de developpement des ressources humaines au Soudan. Selon les termes du document, l'egypte apportera son expertise en matiere de renforcement des capacites et de cooperation technique aux institutions nationales soudanaises.

items.title: Visually impaired student graduates with a first-class degree after relying on friends’ help with notes
items.description: Mariama Fatawu Yambakye, a visually impaired student who relied on her friends to access learning materials throughout her studies, has graduated with a first-class qualification from the Nusrat Jahan Ahmadiyya College of Education (NJA) in Wa. Mariama, who was the only visually impaired student in her batch, said her journey through the College was initially difficult because she lacked a smartphone and laptop to access electronic copies of textbooks and other learning materials. “When I came to this school, I was very sad because I was the only visually impaired student in our batch. I was afraid, and I was just wondering how I would go through this journey alone,” she said. Although lecturers printed copies of the learning materials for her, she could not read them because of her visual impairment. She said the situation made independent study difficult, particularly when her friends were unavailable to assist her. “My big problem was just about me not being able to read myself. Sometimes I always want to study, but because I can’t read on my own, it was difficult for me if my friend is not around to help me,” she said. Her situation changed when she developed a close friendship with Ruhia Abdul-Rahman, who helped her access learning materials and prepare for examinations. Ruhia adopted a method that allowed Mariama to study independently by recording lessons on her phone. Mariama would use her phone to record while Ruhia read and explained the contents of textbooks and other study materials. She would later listen to the recordings to revise. She also sometimes wrote in Braille, which Mr Jambosco, the teacher responsible for visually impaired students, transcribed into ordinary text. One of their biggest challenges came in Level 200 during an Introduction to English Language course, particularly with phonetics and the writing of speech sounds. Ruhia said she sometimes had to guide Mariama physically by holding her hand and helping her use a pen to understand how the symbols were written. “To an extent, I have to hold her hand and then give her a pen so that she will see how it is being drawn,” she explained. Mariama credited Ruhia’s support and commitment for helping her overcome the difficulties and achieve the first-class qualification. “It is through her hard work and then the love that she had for me that made me get this award, because I can’t read on my own,” she said. She also acknowledged the sacrifices and encouragement of her family throughout her education. “My family had to make a lot of sacrifices for me, and then the constant encouragement from them helped me. I appreciate it,” she added. Drawing on her experience, Mariama encouraged other visually impaired students not to give up despite the challenges they may encounter in school. “It’s not easy for us, the visually impaired students. We have to go through a lot of challenges. So I will advise them to also learn hard and make friends, socialise with other people so that they can help them,” she said. Mariama’s achievement was celebrated at the College’s 11th graduation ceremony.

items.title: Portuguese foreign minister arrives in Pakistan for official visit: FO
items.description: Minister of State and Foreign Affairs of Portugal Paulo Rangel arrived in Pakistan on Sunday for an official visit, the Foreign Office (FO) said. Rangel is visiting Pakistan at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar from Nov 22 to 23. He was received upon arrival by Additional Secretary Europe Ambassador Ayesha Ali. According to FO, Rangel will hold delegation-level talks with DPM Dar as well as meetings with Pakistani leadership. “He is accompanied by a business delegation for the inaugural Pakistan-Portugal Business Forum,” FO said, expressing hope that the visit will provide an opportunity to review the full spectrum of the bilateral relationship. Speaking to the media, Rangel praised the peace efforts of Pakistan in recent months during the US-Iran war. “The world needs you. We have been seeing in the very recent months that the role of Pakistan is decisive for global peace, so we count on you to help all the peoples of the world, reaching peace and prosperity,” he told Pakistan TV . The visit comes as Pakistan and Portugal mark the 77th anniversary of their diplomatic relations, established on Nov 7, 1949, FO spokesperson said in a statement on Saturday. The two leaders will review bilateral relations and discuss ways to expand trade and investment. “The visit will also feature a Pakistan-Portugal Business Forum. Companies from both countries will hold business-to-business meetings to explore commercial partnerships and investment opportunities in agri-food, renewable energy, pharmaceuticals, information technology and textiles,” the spokesperson had added in his statement. Foreign Minister Rangel’s visit will provide an opportunity to build on the longstanding ties between Pakistan and Portugal and to broaden bilateral cooperation across diverse sectors.

Le coordinateur de la mission, Abou Obaida Mokhtar, dans une déclaration relayée par l’Agence mauritanienne de presse (officielle), que la campagne vise à offrir 4 000 consultations médicales gratuites, à réaliser 400 opérations chirurgicales de cataracte, ainsi qu’à distribuer 950 paires de lunettes ophtalmologiques et à fournir les médicaments et traitements nécessaires aux patients. Il a ajouté que la mission durera quatre jours et que 21 membres, parmi lesquels des médecins et du personnel médical auxiliaire, y participeront. Il a précisé que les interventions de l’équipe médicale comprennent la chirurgie de la cataracte et la pose de lentilles intraoculaires, le traitement du glaucome, ainsi que la fourniture de consultations médicales concernant diverses maladies oculaires.

items.title: 3 TTP-linked terrorists killed in village on outskirts of Peshawar: CTD
items.description: PESHAWAR: Three terrorists were killed during an exchange of fire with Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and military personnel in the Passani village, located on Peshawar’s outskirts, late on Saturday night, the CTD said in a statement on Sunday. The statement said the CTD received intelligence about the presence of a group of terrorists belonging to Fitna-al-Khawarij on Passani Road — an area located 23 miles south of Peshawar, falling within the jurisdiction of Mattani police station. Fitna-al-Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). The CTD said the terrorists planned to carry out attacks on government installations. “Based on the confirmed reports, CTD’s Special Weapons and Tactics Teams (SWAT), along with personnel of the Pakistan Army, equipped with modern weapons, reached the area to arrest the terrorists,” the statement added. However, upon seeing law enforcement and security personnel, the terrorists opened fire, to which the teams responded effectively in self-defence, the statement further said. Following an exchange of fire, a search operation was launched in the area during which the bodies of three terrorists were found, it said. The CTD identified the terrorists as Abdul Rashid, Saeedullah, and Saeed Nawab — members of the banned TTP. The statement added that other terrorists present at the site managed to escape; meanwhile, the teams recovered two Kalashnikovs, a pistol, three hand grenades, five magazines and computerised national identity cards (CNICs) from the slain terrorists. A search operation was under way to arrest the escaped terrorists, the statement added. As per the CTD statement, KP Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed and Additional IG CTD Jawad Qamar vowed that terrorists would never be allowed to succeed. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif lauded security forces for the successful operation, observing that “timely and decisive action” thwarted a “major threat”, state-run APP reported. The operations of the security forces against terrorism are a reflection of national resolve and morale, the report quoted him as saying. Constable martyred in attack in Lower South Waziristan Separately, a police constable was martyred after unidentified motorcyclists opened fire on him near Mughal Khel village in Wana’s Rustam Bazaar in Lower South Waziristan. The constable, identified as Abdul Salam Dottani, sustained critical bullet injuries in the attack. He was immediately taken to the District Headquarters Hospital in Wana, but succumbed to his injuries despite medical treatment. Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Nadir Khan Wazir confirmed the incident to Dawn over the telephone, saying that unidentified armed men riding a motorcycle had targeted the police constable and fled the scene after the shooting. He said police had registered an initial report and launched an investigation into the incident. Efforts were underway to determine the motive behind the attack and identify those responsible for the killing. The funeral prayers of the martyred constable were offered at the Police Lines in Wana with full official honours. District Police Officer (DPO) Shah Hassan (PSP), Deputy Commissioner Musarrat Zaman, CTD Superintendent of Police (SP) Gul Rauf Khan, Wana Circle DSP Basharat Khan, Birmal DSP Wazir and other senior police officials, personnel and people from different walks of life attended the funeral proceedings. A well-equipped police contingent presented a guard of honour to the deceased, while senior police and civil administration officials laid floral wreaths on his coffin to pay tribute to his services and sacrifice. The participants offered prayers for the departed soul and expressed solidarity with the bereaved family. Police officials paid tribute to Constable Dottani, saying that he had sacrificed his life while performing his official duties. They described his sacrifice as an example of courage, dedication and commitment to public service. The incident comes amid a continued surge in attacks targeting police personnel in Upper and Lower South Waziristan over the past two years. The recurring attacks have raised serious concerns about the security situation in both districts, where police personnel and law enforcement agencies continue to face security challenges. KP continues to actively face terrorist threats. Last week, 43 terrorists were killed during operations conducted in KP, including 35 in Mir Ali, North Waziristan district, and eight in Orakzai district, the military’s media wing said. On the other hand, the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), an Islamabad-based independent think tank monitoring conflict and security developments, has reported encouraging trends in KP in its monthly assessment for October. In mainland KP, PICSS recorded 40 attacks during October, compared with 58 in September, representing a reduction of 31pc. Meanwhile, deaths resulting from these attacks declined from 90 to 38, a decrease of approximately 58pc, while injuries fell from 165 to 19, representing a reduction of 88pc. The merged districts of KP recorded 30 attacks during October, compared with 34 in September, and deaths resulting from these attacks decreased from 33 to 25, while injuries increased from 11 to 13, the report said.

items.title: 70% Local gold refining by 2027 : CLGB highlights key enablers
items.description: The Chamber of Licensed Gold Buyers (CLGB) has underscored the importance of strategic investment in infrastructure, financing and sector formalisation to support Ghana’s ambition of refining 70 per cent of artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) gold locally by December 2027. In its policy position on the 2027 Budget, the Chamber welcomed the Government’s strategic direction to transition Ghana from the export of raw minerals towards greater domestic refining, value addition and industrial development. CLGB considers this ambition a significant opportunity to deepen local participation in the gold value chain, strengthen national economic resilience and maximise the developmental benefits of the country’s mineral resources. The Chamber notes that, based on its current estimates, approximately 30 per cent of ASM gold is refined locally. Achieving the 70 per cent target would therefore require a substantial expansion of domestic refining capacity, alongside the development of an integrated ecosystem capable of supporting efficient, reliable and commercially sustainable operations. CLGB emphasises that the successful delivery of this ambition will depend not only on refinery infrastructure, but also on dependable energy supply, skilled technical personnel, advanced laboratory and assaying facilities, access to affordable financing and a transparent, traceable and responsibly sourced gold supply chain. In this regard, the Chamber encourages the accelerated implementation of GoldBod’s Formalisation and Financing Support Programme, complemented by expanded responsible sourcing initiatives. These interventions, in CLGB’s view, will be instrumental in strengthening the operational capacity of licensed gold buyers, improving traceability and creating more structured pathways for financing and supplying domestic refineries. The Chamber further advocates the development of a comprehensive Ghana Gold Development Plan to provide a coherent, long-term framework for the sector’s transformation. Such a plan should align production, aggregation, refining, financing, infrastructure and export strategy, while ensuring that a meaningful proportion of the economic value generated from Ghana’s gold resources is reinvested in critical national infrastructure, including roads, energy and logistics. CLGB remains committed to working collaboratively with Government, GoldBod, refinery operators, financiers and other industry stakeholders to advance Ghana’s gold value-addition agenda. The Chamber believes that, with the right formalization policy coordination, investment architecture and industry partnerships, Ghana’s 70 per cent local refining ambition can become a catalyst for industrial growth, sustainable employment and greater national value capture from the gold sector. chamber statement on the 2030 ambition ghanas mineral wealth creation Download

items.title: La Gambie obtient gain de cause devant la CIJ pour la plainte pour génocide des rohingya portée contre Myanmar
items.description: La Gambie a remporté une victoire judiciaire devant la Cour internationale de justice, qui a établi jeudi que le Myanmar s'était rendu coupable de génocide à l'encontre de la minorité rohingya en 2017, dans un arrêt qualifié d'« historique » par la présidence gambienne, qui a déclaré que cela faisait de la Gambie le premier pays de l'histoire à obtenir gain de cause dans une affaire de génocide devant cette cour. Le ministre gambien de la Justice, Dauda Jallo, a remis au président Adama Barrow une copie certifiée conforme du jugement, samedi, dans la région d’« Upper River », selon l’annonce de la présidence gambienne. La Cour internationale de justice a statué que le Myanmar avait commis un génocide à l’encontre des Rohingyas dans l’État de Rakhine, au nord du pays, lors des « opérations de nettoyage » menées en 2017, en violation de la Convention pour la prévention et la répression du crime de génocide de 1948. La Cour a ordonné au Myanmar de reconnaître les Rohingyas comme ses citoyens, de faciliter le retour des personnes déplacées dans des conditions sûres, volontaires et dignes, et de verser des indemnités et des réparations à la communauté et à ses membres. La Gambie avait saisi la Cour en novembre 2019 au nom des 57 États membres de l’Organisation de la coopération islamique. Il s’agissait de la première affaire de ce type intentée par un État n’ayant aucun lien direct avec les crimes visés par la Convention pour la prévention et la répression du crime de génocide.

items.title: Ouverture du Dak’art 2026 : La scène s’éveille au rythme de l’ (anti)fragilité
items.description: La cérémonie d’ouverture de la 16e Biennale de l’art africain contemporain, le jeudi 19 novembre à l’Ancien Palais de justice de Dakar, a réservé une place importante aux arts de la scène. La voix d’Oumar Pène, les mouvements de la troupe Bakalama, la création chorégraphique « Dëgërlu, la mue du vivant » et l’apparition du Congolais Fally Ipupa ont donné à cette soirée inaugurale une coloration musicale et chorégraphique, entre ancrage sénégalais et ouverture congolaise. À l’Ancien Palais de justice de Dakar, l’art a également trouvé son expression dans la voix, le rythme et le mouvement des corps. Pour accompagner l’ouverture de la 16e Biennale de Dakar, le jeudi 19 novembre 2026, la scène est restée tout au long de la soirée, un espace de rencontres entre plusieurs univers musicaux et chorégraphiques. Trois moments ont particulièrement marqué cette séquence artistique, avec des propositions qui ont placé la musique et la danse au cœur de la célébration. Oumar Pène a donné le premier ton avec « Sénégal ». Accompagné de la troupe « Bakalama », le chanteur a porté sur scène une chanson qui fait de l’attachement au pays et de la paix son fil conducteur. Sa voix, familière aux amateurs de musique sénégalaise, a ouvert cette parenthèse artistique sous le signe d’un message collectif. Le choix de ce titre a aussi inscrit la prestation dans une dimension symbolique, au moment où Dakar accueille des artistes et des délégations venues de différents horizons. La présence du groupe « Bakalama » a apporté une matière particulière à cette interprétation. La danse est ainsi venue accompagner la voix et inscrire le rythme dans une expression corporelle. Cette première séquence a magistralement associé deux langages artistiques, la chanson et le mouvement, dans une mise en valeur du patrimoine musical sénégalais. Oumar Pène a porté le message par la voix, tandis que les danseurs ont contribué à sa traduction scénique. Le programme a ensuite pris une orientation chorégraphique avec « Dëgërlu, la mue du vivant ». Le titre, qui convoque l’idée de transformation, place le vivant au centre de la proposition artistique. La création a réuni la troupe Bakalama et le chanteur Woz Kaly, sous la mise en scène de Madiaw Ndiaye. « M’bote na yoo » La rencontre entre ces artistes a ouvert un espace où la danse et la musique se sont répondues et ont participé à une co-construction scénique. Le mouvement porte une intention artistique, la musique accompagne l’expression et le titre donne une clé de lecture autour de la métamorphose. « Dëgërlu, la mue du vivant » s’inscrit ainsi dans une recherche autour des transformations, des cycles et des formes de vie. Cette présence de la danse dans la cérémonie rappelle également la diversité des disciplines que la Biennale rassemble autour de la création contemporaine africaine. Avec la voix singulière et mythique de Woz Kaly, la pièce performative a pris part à une création pensée autour du dialogue entre le mouvement et la musique. Deux cadres artistiques qui ont donné, en a plus douter, à voir différentes possibilités d’expression du corps sur scène. La République démocratique du Congo, pays invité d’honneur de cette édition, a également apporté sa signature musicale à la cérémonie avec Fally Ipupa. L’artiste congolais a effectué une courte prestation devant le public. Sa présence a inscrit la scène dakaroise dans une autre géographie musicale, celle d’une musique congolaise dont le rayonnement dépasse largement les frontières nationales. Cette intervention a prolongé le dialogue entre les cultures qui traversait le programme artistique. Après la chanson sénégalaise et la création chorégraphique portée par des artistes du pays, l’apparition de Fally Ipupa a donné une place à la scène congolaise. Un clin d’œil à la République démocratique du Congo (Rdc), dont la participation en tant qu’invité d’honneur, occupe une place particulière dans cette 16e édition. La succession de ces prestations a donné à la soirée inaugurale une composition artistique faite de voix, de rythmes et de mouvements. À travers ces propositions, la cérémonie a rappelé la place des arts vivants dans les grandes rencontres consacrées à la création africaine. La musique, la danse et la performance ont ainsi accompagné l’entrée de Dak’Art dans une nouvelle édition, avec le Sénégal et la République démocratique du Congo réunis sur une même scène. Amadou KÉBÉ

items.title: La coopération agricole mauritano-chinoise évoquée par le ministre en charge du département avec l’ambassadeur de Chine à Nouakchott
items.description: Le ministre mauritanien de l'Agriculture et de la Sécurité alimentaire, Ahmed Baba Eleya, a examiné samedi à Nouakchott, avec une délégation chinoise de la province du Heilongjiang, conduite par le vice-gouverneur de la province, Yu Jian, les moyens de renforcer la coopération agricole entre les deux pays. Le ministère a indiqué, dans un message publié sur sa page Facebook, que la rencontre avait porté sur les perspectives de renforcement du partenariat bilatéral et d’élargissement des domaines de coopération, notamment dans les domaines liés au développement agricole, à la mise en valeur des terres et à l’échange d’expertise et d’expériences. Les deux parties ont également discuté des moyens de tirer parti de leurs potentialités et de leurs expertises respectives, afin de contribuer à soutenir les efforts de développement agricole. L'ambassadeur de Chine en Mauritanie, Tang Zhongdong, ainsi que le secrétaire général du ministère de l'Agriculture et plusieurs responsables du secteur ont assisté à cette rencontre.

items.title: La Mauritanie a exposé à l’OMI ses besoins en matière de coopération technique avec cette organisation
items.description: Le directeur général de l'Agence mauritanienne des affaires maritimes, Cheikh Ahmedou Sidi, a exposé au secrétaire général de l'Organisation maritime internationale les besoins de la Mauritanie en matière de coopération technique, de même que les priorités des pays francophones d'Afrique occidentale et centrale. L'Agence mauritanienne des affaires maritimes a indiqué, dans un communiqué publié hier samedi, que la rencontre s'était tenue le 17 novembre dernier, en marge de la 9e conférence de l'Association des administrations maritimes africaines (AAMA), qui s'est tenue à Kampala, la capitale ougandaise, et à laquelle le directeur général a participé en sa qualité de président du groupe de travail de l'AAMA pour les pays francophones d'Afrique de l'Ouest et de l'Afrique centrale. L’agence a ajouté que les discussions ont porté sur la mise en conformité avec les conventions internationales adoptées dans le cadre de l’Organisation maritime internationale (OMI) et sur l’intégration de leurs dispositions dans les législations nationales, ainsi que sur la formation des marins et la délivrance de leurs certificats, la mise en œuvre de la convention relative à la formation, aux certificats et aux quarts du personnel des navires de pêche, ainsi que l’offre de stages de formation à bord des navires dans le cadre du programme « NextWave Seafarers ». Les discussions ont également porté sur les stratégies maritimes nationales, la numérisation des administrations, l’audit des États membres de l’OMI et la réduction des émissions de carbone dans le secteur maritime. L’Agence a indiqué que le secrétaire général de l’Organisation avait salué cette initiative et manifesté la volonté de l’Organisation de soutenir les activités proposées par le biais d’une coopération technique, tout en exprimant son espoir que celle-ci serve de modèle à d’autres régions.

items.title: Naqvi hits back at minister for repeated criticism: report
items.description: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has hit back at a federal minister for what he said was repeated criticism against him, Geo News reported on Sunday. The news website reported that Naqvi, without naming the minister, claimed the latter had been commenting on him on television almost every day to “gain attention”. The report described the remarks as part of an informal conversation with Geo News and further quoted Naqvi as saying that he had been patiently listening to the minister’s statements for the past two-and-a-half years — the tenure of the incumbent government since the 2024 elections. “The day I comment on this minister, he will not be able to show his face,” Naqvi warned, according to the outlet. Naqvi also defended the businesspeople present at an economic forum who he said were criticised by the minister. He said the attendees were respectable citizens who had served as presidents and office-bearers of chambers of commerce at the federal and city levels, according to the report. While the report did not quote him as mentioning any specific details in this connection, Naqvi’s remarks at the Pakistan Economic Summit in Islamabad in July had been making headlines in recent months. Naqvi had whipped up a political storm by calling for creating new administrative units in the country to “reset” the current “system” of governance while speaking at the forum, which was attended by businessmen. In his remarks to Geo News , Naqvi stated that the businessmen were also among the country’s highest taxpayers. “If these businessmen are so bad, why do you take billions of rupees from them in the name of party funds at every election?” the interior minister was quoted as saying. Naqvi’s remarks have been reported a day after Inter-Provincial Coordination Minister Rana Sanaullah questioned the objectives of some of the businesspeople at that July forum. In an interview on Geo News programme ‘Jirga’ aired on Saturday, Sanaullah said the “matter got worse in such a way that the debate on provinces began from an economic forum” and Naqvi started the discussion. Sanaullah, also Naqvi’s predecessor, contended that there were “some objectionable businessmen sitting among the audience of that economic forum”. “It has been their background that in each tenure, they keep on telling the incoming ruler, especially the army chief, that ‘sir, the whole world is looking at you and only you are the saviour,’” Sanaullah said. The PML-N leader clarified that he was not referring to the entire business community, but rather “a few people who keep committing crime in business, and here as well”. On differing stances among federal cabinet members on the issue of new provinces, Sanaullah contended that politicians could express their opinions, as “regimental discipline” could not be brought into the cabinet. Sanaullah stressed that the debate on provinces was “not wrong”, but he contended that the “debate was being entangled with other matters; saying that the system has collapsed; after that some remarks were made about the prime minister, and similarly about politicians contesting elections in so and so manner”. The PML-N leader also criticised PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari for further complicating the situation by referring to various matters in his Nov 17 speech, rather than merely voicing his objection to carving out new administrative units out of Sindh. Sanaullah further termed both Bilawal and Naqvi as “sons” of President Asif Ali Zardari, adding that they were “under his discipline”. Asked about the independent senator being “under President Zardari’s discipline”, Sanaullah reiterated, “Yes, definitely. He has not disowned him yet. He himself calls him (Naqvi) his son; it is not that we are saying so.” Referring to a recent meeting between President Zardari and PM Shehbaz Sharif, during which Naqvi was also present, Sanaullah said a “ceasefire was decided” there. He claimed that, according to information he had, a meeting was held at President House recently, which was attended by President Zardari, Bilawal and Naqvi, and it was decided to reduce tensions. Replying to a query about the independent senator, Sanaullah remarked that Naqvi was a senator of both PPP and PML-N, as leaders from both parties contributed to the votes for his election. In September as well, Sanaullah had said that the “debate should have been started in Parliament”, adding that issues of such magnitude should not be reduced to speeches, social media, seminars or business forums. The PML-N leader has also taken jibes at the interior minister on a few other occasions since the ruling coalition came to power. On the other hand, Sindh Local Government Minister Nasir Hussain Shah also took exception to Sanaullah’s remarks, asserting that Bilawal was the only son of President Zardari. “Mohsin Naqvi sahib is worthy of respect in his place, but nothing about him compares to the chairman (Bilawal),” he told reporters . Shah maintained there was “no such thing” as suggested by the PML-N minister, declaring, “There is only one Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, and only his words will prevail here.”

items.title: Hommage à Petit Sory : Le Gouvernement organise un symposium en son honneur
items.description: Le gouvernement guinéen a organisé ce dimanche 22 novembre 2026 un symposium pour rendre un ultime hommage à Petit Sory, décédé le 21 novembre. La cérémonie a réuni des membres du gouvernement, d'anciennes gloires du football guinéen, membres de la famille et proches collaborateurs du défunt. Le ministre des Sports, Cellou Baldé, a présenté les condoléances des autorités à la famille éplorée : « Je suis là au nom du gouvernement de la République, au nom du Premier ministre, Chef du gouvernement Monsieur Amadou Oury Bah, au nom du président de la République, Son Excellence Monsieur Mamadi Doumbouya, pour présenter solennellement et officiellement, les condoléances du Président, du gouvernement et de l'ensemble des institutions de la République à la famille biologique et sportive de feu Petit Sory. » Lors du symposium, il a placé Petit Sory et ses coéquipiers dans la lignée des grandes figures de l'histoire nationale : « Petit Sory et ses coéquipiers, pour moi, c'est comme ceux qui nous ont conduits vers l'indépendance. C'est comme Almamy Samory Touré, c'est comme Zébela Togba Pivi, c'est comme Dinah Salifou, c'est comme Alpha Yaya Diallo, parce que la fibre, elle est la même : c'est la patrie. C'est ce qui les a animés. » Il a insisté sur la portée des exploits des anciens du Hafia : « La période post-indépendance pendant laquelle les anciens du Hafia ont posé ces actes héroïques, c'était une période particulière. Période pendant laquelle ces actes héroïques posés n'étaient pas qu'un simple jeu de sport ou de football. Cela nous a permis de renforcer notre souveraineté et d'asseoir davantage la respectabilité de notre pays à l'échelle continentale et internationale, parce que c'était aussi un enjeu politique et un enjeu géopolitique » Il a ensuite lancé : « Et donc, la Guinée ne saurait oublier Petit Sory. La Guinée ne saurait oublier toutes ces gloires, tous ces amis et coéquipiers de Petit Sory. » Cellou Baldé a par ailleurs indiqué que les doléances formulées lors de la rencontre par les anciennes gloires du Hafia avaient été entendues : « Nous avons aussi écouté attentivement. Nous avons compris toutes les doléances formulées. Nous allons travailler à les mettre en œuvre au niveau du ministère des Sports, en relation bien entendu avec la Fédération guinéenne de football, mais nous transmettrons fidèlement les doléances au Premier ministre, chef du gouvernement, et au président de la République », a-t-il laissé entendre. Il a enfin fait le lien entre l'hommage rendu aux anciens et l'action actuelle des autorités. « Si aujourd'hui nous sommes en train de jouer au stade du 28-Septembre, c'est aussi une manière de rendre hommage aux anciens du Hafia 77. […] C'est le rayonnement de la Guinée, c'est le Hafia 77 qui revit aujourd'hui », a-t-il conclu.

items.title: Importante attaque du JNIM contre l’armée malienne et le corps africain russe dans le centre du Mali
items.description: Le groupe « Nasra al-Islam wa al-Muslimin » a attaqué samedi au moins deux positions de l'armée malienne et des forces relevant du Corps africain russe dans la région de Ségou, au centre du pays, faisant plusieurs victimes dans les rangs de l'armée, selon Radio France Internationale. La radio a indiqué que les assaillants étaient arrivés à moto, en véhicule et à pied, et qu’ils avaient pris pour cible des positions militaires stratégiques dans la région de Niouno, où de violents affrontements ont eu lieu et où des véhicules incendiés ont été aperçus à l’intérieur d’un des camps. Elle a ajouté que le groupe avait qualifié le bilan de l’attaque d’important, tandis que l’armée malienne a mis en doute les chiffres annoncés. Par ailleurs, un engin explosif « de fabrication artisanale » a détruit un véhicule blindé appartenant à la Légion africaine dans la même région. De son côté, l’état-major général des forces armées maliennes a annoncé ce dimanche avoir mené samedi trois vagues de frappes aériennes aux alentours de Niouno, visant des positions des assaillants au nord-est, au sud et au nord de la ville. Il a indiqué que ces frappes avaient permis de neutraliser quatre combattants et de détruire entièrement une camionnette, tout en ciblant des positions abritant des combattants, du matériel de guerre et des ravitaillements logistiques. L’état-major a ajouté que les opérations de surveillance et de reconnaissance se poursuivaient aux abords de Niouno afin d’évaluer les résultats des frappes, de rechercher les combattants en fuite pour les neutraliser.

items.title: Accra Academy 2001 Year Group marks 25th anniversary; hands over renovated dining hall, kitchen complex
items.description: The Accra Academy 2001 Year Group, popularly known as BLEOO 2G1, has marked its 25th anniversary with the official handover and commissioning of a renovated Dining Hall and Kitchen Complex at the school. The ceremony, held on Saturday, 14 November 2026, at the forecourt of the Dining Hall, brought together old students, school authorities, corporate partners, guests and members of the Accra Academy community to celebrate a significant investment in the school’s infrastructure. The renovation project, undertaken by the 2001 Year Group with the support of Star Oil Ghana Limited as the main corporate sponsor, represents the group’s commitment to giving back to its alma mater and improving the welfare of current and future students. A Legacy Beyond Celebration Rather than limiting its silver jubilee celebration to social activities and reunions, the 2001 Year Group chose to commemorate the milestone by undertaking a lasting infrastructure project that would directly benefit the school. The initiative focused on upgrading the Dining Hall and Kitchen Complex to provide a more comfortable, functional and improved environment for students and kitchen staff. The Dining Hall underwent extensive refurbishment, including the replacement of ceiling materials, doors, lighting fixtures and fans, as well as improvements to the interior and exterior finishes. Additional works included the replacement of corridor guardrails, installation of interior railings, rehabilitation of the entrance sheds, concreting of the forecourt, landscaping and the improvement of pedestrian pathways. The kitchen facilities also received significant attention, with upgrades designed to improve food preparation, staff welfare and operational efficiency. These included the provision of modern food steamers, improvements to cooking and food preparation areas, water storage facilities, and the renovation and expansion of staff changing and accommodation facilities. The project is expected to improve the daily dining experience of students while providing a more conducive working environment for the school’s catering personnel. Star Oil Ghana Limited Supports the Vision A major highlight of the project was the partnership between the Accra Academy 2001 Year Group and Star Oil Ghana Limited, whose sponsorship played an important role in bringing the initiative to fruition. The involvement of Star Oil demonstrates the positive impact that collaboration between alumni associations and corporate organisations can have on educational infrastructure development. The company’s Chief Executive Officer, Mr. Phillip Tieku, was identified to lead the official commissioning of the renovated facility. The project also benefited from the support of other partners, including Furnart Ghana Limited, which contributed towards the improvement of the facility through its support for the doors component of the renovation. The 2001 Year Group acknowledged the importance of these partnerships in translating its anniversary vision into a tangible legacy. A Celebration of Brotherhood and Service The handover ceremony provided an opportunity for members of the 2001 Year Group to reflect on their journey since leaving Accra Academy 25 years ago. What began as a shared educational experience has developed into a lasting network of friendship, professional achievement and collective responsibility. The event also highlighted the role alumni associations can play in supporting educational institutions through coordinated fundraising, professional expertise, partnerships and volunteerism. The ceremony brought attention to the contributions of the project’s planning and implementation committees, alumni donors, corporate sponsors and individuals who supported the initiative. The occasion reinforced the enduring bond between Accra Academy and its old students, demonstrating that the values of discipline, excellence and service continue to influence graduates long after they leave the school. Investing in the Next Generation Beyond its physical improvements, the renovated Dining Hall and Kitchen Complex represents an investment in the wellbeing of the next generation of Accra Academy students. A functional dining facility is an essential part of the boarding-school experience, contributing to student welfare, hygiene and the effective delivery of meals. By prioritising this project, BLEOO 2G1 has demonstrated that alumni celebrations can serve a broader developmental purpose and create benefits that extend well beyond the anniversary year. The initiative also offers an example of how old students’ associations can work with corporate institutions to address infrastructure needs within Ghana’s educational sector. Leaving a Lasting Legacy For the Accra Academy 2001 Year Group, the completion and handover of the Dining Hall and Kitchen Complex is more than the conclusion of an anniversary project. It is a demonstration of gratitude to an institution that helped shape its members and a commitment to ensuring that future generations enjoy improved facilities. The project embodies the spirit of the group’s 25th anniversary celebration and its enduring message: “ We Came as Boys. We Return as Brothers. We Leave a Legacy. ” As the renovated facility begins a new chapter of service to the Accra Academy community, the 2001 Year Group’s contribution stands as a reminder that the true measure of an alumni association lies not only in the strength of its brotherhood but also in the lasting impact it creates. ESSE QUAM VIDERI — To Be Rather Than to Seem.

items.title: The World’s Biggest Climate Conference Just Fell Apart
items.description: If for nothing else, the United Nations’ annual climate gathering can be useful for focusing world leaders’ attention on the fate of the planet for a week or two. During this year’s conference, though, Presidents Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin were instead meeting with one another in China, where they agreed to increase oil production; only one G7 leader, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, showed up in Antalya, Turkey, where the UN conference, known as COP 31, was held. When a world leader did appear at the conference, a media scrum would form, Marek Pruszewicz, a former BBC editor who now runs the climate publication Dialogue Earth , told me. But when the leaders left, reporters seemed to vanish just as quickly. He saw television journalists working amid empty seats and rows of vacant press tables. “It’s just not cutting through,” Pruszewicz said. The same could be said of the year’s biggest climate fight in the United States, over a permitting-reform bill that the Senate passed on Thursday. Proponents argue that the bill is necessary for clean energy to thrive; opponents see it as a gift to gas companies. If you talk with people involved in this debate, or dip into the corners of social media where the issues are being litigated out loud, you’ll still find vehement arguments about the fate of the planet. But it’s hard to shake the feeling that the world seems to care less about solving this problem than it once did. On Sunday, the COP negotiations collapsed for only the third time in the conference’s 30-year history. The world’s diplomats spent more than 20 years at these climate negotiations before they agreed to even mention fossil fuels, the dominant driver of global warming, as part of the problem. That happened five years ago, at the UN climate summit in Glasgow, when negotiators agreed not on a “phase out” but on just a “phase down” of the use of coal. The following year, in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt, dozens of countries pressed for an agreement to “phase down” all fossil fuels; only in 2023, in Dubai, did diplomats commit to the more effervescent idea of a “transitioning away.” The negotiations over the past two weeks in Antalya made those past efforts sound ambitious, even idealistic. During the talks this week, negotiators stripped out all references to fossil fuels and to reducing the world’s dependence on them from a draft agreement. The negotiators also cut references to the historical responsibility of developed countries for causing climate change. Mohamed Adow, the director of Power Shift Africa, a climate-advocacy group, told reporters on Friday that this has been “the worst COP ever.” The negotiations ran into overtime, as negotiators tried to land on an agreement that could gain the necessary consensus to pass, but on Sunday, they admitted that they had failed. The signature proposal, set by the host nation at the conference’s outset, was to set a goal of increasing the proportion of electrification of the world’s energy consumption from 23 percent, where it is now, to 35 percent by 2035. This shift is seen as important for eventually lowering carbon emissions, by switching out internal-combusion cars and oil heaters with electric alternatives, which can be more efficient even if their electricity comes from power plants burning fossil fuels. Reaching “35 by 35” would not be easy—it would require a more than fourfold speedup in the pace of electrification—but hitting that goal still wouldn’t keep the atmosphere from warming 2 or more degrees Celsius from the baseline before the Industrial Revolution. That amounts to “catastrophic global warming,” Johan Rockström, the director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, told me from Antalya last week. The electrification goal, he said, was, to begin with, a “minor and insufficient consolation.” Ultimately, the negotiations broke down in part over the question of whether the agreement would mention fossil fuels at all. Some environmentalists worry that Congress, too, is too willing to ignore the problem of fossil fuels’ future. The bipartisan permitting bill, which will now head to the House, would rewrite bedrock environmental laws to speed up the build-out of transmission lines and new sources of clean energy. But these laws would also make it easier to build all sorts of infrastructure, including (opponents point out) gas pipelines, data centers, and ICE-detention centers, as well as (proponents note) ecological-restoration projects. Like COP’s organizers, the architects of this bill see it as a practical measure that will continue advancing climate goals. One of its sponsors is Senator Sheldon Whitehouse, who has been one of the most consistent advocates for climate policy in Congress. The bill’s supporters argue that it clears the way for clean energy to continue its takeover, even if, in the short term, the bill also helps the fossil-fuel industry. (Opponents see fossil-fuel companies as better positioned to take advantage of any new build-out.) Some former Biden-administration staffers believe that the bill could fix a problem they ran into with their signature climate legislation: They made it easier to build solar and wind farms, but not easier to build the power lines to connect them to anything. No one thinks that the bill does enough, on its own, to dramatically change the trajectory of U.S. emissions; people on both sides of the argument fear a future in which the status quo sticks. Climate scientists are taking encouragement where they can. If the biggest climate fights of 2027 will be focused on limited “practical” questions, then so will the clearest advances: The use of solar- and other renewable-energy sources is growing. So is the adoption of EVs. Both are happening far faster in many other countries than they are in the United States. Still, the reminders about the costs of continued warming were hard to miss this year: the glacier collapse in Nepal that swept away more than 1,500 people. The summer heat wave in Europe that killed some 50,000 more. The El Niño in an already overheated Pacific Ocean that’s spinning out droughts and floods around the world. Climate scientists say the goal of keeping warming below 1.5 degrees Celsius will inevitably be surpassed; the latest report by the World Meteorological Organization found that global mean temperatures from January to September were 1.47 degrees Celsius above preindustrial levels. Celeste Saulo, the WMO secretary general, told reporters last week that the past dozen years have been the warmest on record, and the past four, including 2026, were the warmest of those. “There is no end in sight,” she said. The question has moved to how bad the “overshoot” period will be and what can be done to minimize the damage and avoid tipping points. “That includes your large ice sheets melting, glaciers melting,” Rachel Cleetus, the climate-program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists, told me. “Once that happens, you can’t bring them back.” The mood going into COP was “pretty somber,” she said, in a year when climate disasters have piled up and fossil-fuel companies reported record profits. She had left for Antalya from Boston amid fall temperatures in the 70s Fahrenheit. By the time the COP talks ended with little to show, most everyone had gone home, and the mood was grim.

items.title: NDC-USA elects new executives to steer chapter’s affairs
items.description: The United States chapter of the National Democratic Congress (NDC-USA) has elected new executives to lead the organisation and strengthen its structures across the country. The election was held on November 14, 2026, during the chapter’s official election and conference at the Marriott Orlando Airport Lakeside Hotel in Orlando, Florida. Dr Joshua N. Quaye was elected Chairman, with Dr Nat Abotchie elected as Vice Chairman. Other elected officers include Labib Sarikin Samari as Secretary, Rashid Awudu as Deputy Secretary for Administration, Dr Bernard Akalebo as Deputy Secretary for Operations, Janet Akweley Wilson as Organiser and Abu Moro as Deputy Organiser. In the Communications Department, Rashad Abdulai was elected Communication Officer, with Dr Francis Kwami Dzikpe as his deputy. The Women’s Wing will be led by Kausar Amid Guinko as Women’s Organiser, supported by Patricia Renee Gomez as Deputy Women’s Organiser. Samuel Osei Tutu, PhD, was elected Treasurer, while Dr Prosper Torku, DBA, will serve as Deputy Treasurer. For the Youth Wing, Dr Gamji Rabiu Abu-Ba’are was elected Youth Organiser, with Ebenezer Mercer as Deputy Youth Organiser. Alhaji Muntari Yahya was also elected Zongo Caucus Coordinator. Five members were elected to serve as other executive members. They are Noble L. Alexander III, Dr Bright Bansah, Hannah Sunday, Kofi Gamor and Atankugu Asaana. Call for unity The conference also provided an opportunity for the outgoing Chairman, Dr Maame Aba Dadzie, and the incoming Chairman, Dr Joshua N. Quaye, to reaffirm their commitment to working together to advance the chapter’s interests. Both leaders stressed the need for unity and cooperation among members, noting that sustained collaboration would be critical to the chapter’s growth and success. In her remarks, Dr Dadzie acknowledged the contributions of the various branch chairmen, saying their efforts had played an important role in the chapter’s achievements. She also highlighted the role of the Council of Elders in supporting the chapter and contributing to its successes. The outgoing chairman urged members to support the newly elected executives and provide them with the necessary backing to build on the chapter’s achievements and take it to greater heights. The election ushers in a new leadership era for NDC-USA, with the incoming executives expected to continue efforts to strengthen the party’s presence among Ghanaians in the United States and the wider diaspora.
